items.title: Grammar 1–3

grammarPages.titleEnglish: Introduce Someone with 叫, 姓, and 是
grammarPages.learnerPromise: Introduce someone by name, surname, or identity.
grammarPages.explanation: 叫 comes before a name. 姓 comes before a family name only. 是 says who someone is.

teachingGlossary.meaning: is called; comes before a given or full name
has the surname; comes before a family name

grammarPages.pattern: Subject + 叫／姓／是 + Noun

discoveryLab.title: Change the word, change the clue
discoveryLab.description: Each sentence introduces the same person. Each word answers a different question.
discoveryLab.prompt: What do you want to say about her?

choices.label: Her name
choices.english: Her name is Xiaolin Youmei.
choices.note: 叫 comes before a given name or a full name.

choices.label: Her surname
choices.english: Her surname is Xiaolin.
choices.note: 姓 only tells the family name. Do not put a full name after it.

choices.label: Who she is
choices.english: She is the new classmate.
choices.note: 是 says who she is. It does not come before a personal name.

discoveryLab.takeaway: Ask yourself: name, family name, or who they are? The answer tells you which word to use: 叫, 姓, or 是.

ruleContrast.title: Family name only after 姓
ruleContrast.description: A full name needs 叫. 姓 stops after the family-name part.

examples.label: Full name after 姓
examples.explanation: 張小明 is a full name. Use 叫 for a full name.

examples.label: Full name
examples.explanation: 叫 comes before the full name.

examples.label: Family name
examples.explanation: 姓 comes before only 張, the family name.

patternRows.english: His name is Zhongming.
Whose surname is Li?
He is not Taiwanese.

items.question: Which word goes before a person’s NAME?
items.answer: 叫. It tells people what someone is called. 是 cannot introduce a name.

right.english: Her name is Xiaolin Youmei.

items.question: Does 姓 take the whole name or one part?
items.answer: One part only — the family name. 姓 stops before the given name.

right.english: Her surname is Xiaolin.

items.question: So what is 是 for?
items.answer: It says who someone IS — a job, a group, a country. Never a name after it.

right.english: He is not Taiwanese.

text.traditional: A：她是誰？ B：她是新同學。
text.simplified: A：她是谁？ B：她是新同学。
text.pinyin: A: Tā shì shéi?  B: Tā shì xīn tóngxué.
text.english: A: Who is she? B: She is a new classmate.

text.traditional: 她是日本人，她不是台灣人。
text.simplified: 她是日本人，她不是台湾人。
text.pinyin: Tā shì Rìběn rén, tā bú shì Táiwān rén.
text.english: She is Japanese. She is not Taiwanese.

text.traditional: 她不姓李，她姓小林，叫小林友美。
text.simplified: 她不姓李，她姓小林，叫小林友美。
text.pinyin: Tā bú xìng Lǐ, tā xìng Xiǎolín, jiào Xiǎolín Yǒuměi.
text.english: Her surname is not Li. Her surname is Xiaolin, and her name is Xiaolin Youmei.

grammarPages.titleEnglish: Describe Someone with 很 or 不
grammarPages.learnerPromise: Say that someone is or is not busy, tired, pretty, or cute.
grammarPages.explanation: 漂亮, 忙, and 累 already carry the meaning "is." Use 很 to say it in a normal, positive way. Use 不 to say it is not true. Do not put 是 before these words.

teachingGlossary.meaning: very; the usual link before a describing word, often softer than English "very"
not; says the next word is not true
is; do not use it before 漂亮, 忙, or 累

grammarPages.pattern: S + 很/不 + Vs

discoveryLab.title: Do not add 是
discoveryLab.description: Tap the middle word and watch the meaning change. In Chinese, the describing word already includes the "is."
discoveryLab.prompt: How does the speaker see her?

choices.label: Positive · 很
choices.english: She is cute.
choices.note: 很 is the normal way to say the description. In everyday sentences it often sounds softer than English "very."

choices.label: Negative · 不
choices.english: She is not cute.
choices.note: 不 takes the place of 很 and sits directly before the describing word: 不 + 可愛.

choices.label: Repair · no 是
choices.traditional: 她是可愛。 → 她很可愛。
choices.simplified: 她是可爱。 → 她很可爱。
choices.pinyin: Tā shì kě'ài. → Tā hěn kě'ài.
choices.english: Repair it: She is cute.
choices.note: Remove 是. 是 is for saying who someone is. 可愛 already describes her.

discoveryLab.takeaway: Say who someone is with 是. Describe them with 很 or 不. Do not mix the two.

patternRows.english: She is (very) pretty.

items.question: English says "she IS pretty." Why is 她是漂亮 wrong?
items.answer: Words like 漂亮 already carry the "is." 很 takes that middle spot; 是 does not.

right.english: She is pretty.

items.question: Why add 很 when it means "very"?
items.answer: A describing word alone can sound unfinished, like you are comparing. 很 is the normal calm link.

right.english: She is pretty.

items.question: How do I say she is NOT busy?
items.answer: Put 不 right before the describing word. 是 has no job here at all.

right.english: She is not busy.

text.traditional: 她很可愛。
text.simplified: 她很可爱。
text.pinyin: Tā hěn kě'ài.
text.english: She is very cute.

text.pinyin: Wáng xiānsheng hěn máng.
text.english: Mr. Wang is very busy.

text.simplified: 我们不累，王太太很累。
text.pinyin: Wǒmen bú lèi, Wáng tàitai hěn lèi.
text.english: We are not tired; Mrs. Wang is very tired.

grammarPages.titleEnglish: Ask a Yes/No Question with 嗎
grammarPages.learnerPromise: Turn a sentence into a natural yes-or-no question.
grammarPages.explanation: Keep the whole sentence in its original order. Add 嗎 at the end. Now the listener answers yes or no. Nothing inside the sentence moves.

teachingGlossary.meaning: ending word that turns a sentence into a yes/no question

grammarPages.pattern: Statement + 嗎

discoveryLab.title: One small ending turns it into a question
discoveryLab.description: The sentence stays exactly the same. Only the ending changes.

choices.label: Tell · sentence
choices.english: She is cute.
choices.note: The full stop means you are telling.

choices.label: Check · + 嗎
choices.english: Is she cute?
choices.note: Add 嗎 after the same sentence. In English the word order changes; in Chinese it does not.

choices.label: Avoid English order
choices.traditional: 嗎她很可愛？ → 她很可愛嗎？
choices.simplified: 吗她很可爱？ → 她很可爱吗？
choices.pinyin: Ma tā hěn kě'ài? → Tā hěn kě'ài ma?
choices.english: Move 嗎 to the end.
choices.note: 嗎 never comes first. Say the sentence first, then put 嗎 at the end.

discoveryLab.takeaway: Sentence first, 嗎 last. If the sentence works on its own, your question is almost done.

patternRows.english: Is he Taiwanese?
Is she pretty?

items.question: Where does 嗎 go — first like "Do you…?" or last?
items.answer: Last. Say the whole sentence, then add 嗎. English flips the order; Chinese does not.

right.english: Is he Japanese?

items.question: Can I use 嗎 together with a question word like 誰?
items.answer: No. A question word already does the asking. Adding 嗎 makes the sentence ask twice.

right.english: Who is he?

items.question: When I answer, do I keep 嗎?
items.answer: No. Drop 嗎 and say the plain sentence. 嗎 is only for asking.

right.english: He is not Japanese.

text.traditional: A：他是日本人嗎？ B：他不是日本人，他是台灣人。
text.simplified: A：他是日本人吗？ B：他不是日本人，他是台湾人。
text.pinyin: A: Tā shì Rìběn rén ma? B: Tā bú shì Rìběn rén, tā shì Táiwān rén.
text.english: A: Is he Japanese? B: No, he is not Japanese. He is Taiwanese.

text.traditional: 高先生叫家樂嗎？
text.simplified: 高先生叫家乐吗？
text.pinyin: Gāo xiānsheng jiào Jiālè ma?
text.english: Is Mr. Gao called Jiale?

text.traditional: 他忙嗎？
text.simplified: 他忙吗？
text.pinyin: Tā máng ma?
text.english: Is he busy?

items.title: Grammar 4–5

grammarPages.titleEnglish: Use 呢 to Say “And You?”
grammarPages.learnerPromise: Ask the same question back with 呢, without repeating the whole sentence.
grammarPages.explanation: When everyone already knows the question, 呢 passes it to another person. Say the new person or thing, then add 呢.

teachingGlossary.meaning: ending word that returns the question; “and you?”
yes/no question ending word; makes a new question
you; the person who receives the question

grammarPages.pattern: Statement, + new topic + 呢

discoveryLab.title: 呢 works like a conversation echo
discoveryLab.description: The short ending word stays the same. The question it repeats changes with what was just said.
discoveryLab.prompt: What are the speakers talking about?

choices.label: Country
choices.pinyin: Wǒ shì Rìběn rén, nǐ ne?
choices.english: I am Japanese. And you?
choices.note: The hidden question is “Which country are you from?” 呢 passes that question to 你.

choices.label: Name
choices.english: My name is Youmei. And you?
choices.note: Now the hidden question is “What is your name?” 呢 keeps that question without repeating it.

choices.label: What you like
choices.english: I like Taiwan. How about you?
choices.note: The listener knows the question is “Do you like Taiwan?” because 喜歡臺灣 was just said.

choices.label: Needs context
choices.english: And you?
choices.note: This works only when the last sentence makes the question clear. Without that, 呢 has nothing to repeat.

discoveryLab.takeaway: Think of 呢 as a shortcut: keep the active question, change the person, and do not repeat the whole sentence.

complement.meaning: ending word that returns the question

patternRows.english: I am Taiwanese. How about you?

complement.meaning: ending word that returns the question

patternRows.english: Yiwen's surname is Wang. How about Zhongming?

contrast.title: 嗎 or 呢?
contrast.description: Both sit at the end of questions, but they do different jobs.

items.label: Ask a new yes/no question
items.note: 嗎 turns the statement before it into a yes/no question.

items.label: Ask the same question back
items.pinyin: Wǒ shì Rìběn rén, nǐ ne?
items.english: I am Japanese. How about you?
items.note: 呢 avoids repeating “Which country are you from?”

microChecks.prompt: The first speaker already said their country. Which ending word asks it back?
microChecks.explanation: 呢 means “and you?” because the country question was already asked.

microChecks.prompt: No country question has been asked yet. Which ending word makes a new yes/no question?
microChecks.explanation: 嗎 turns the complete statement into a new yes/no question.

items.question: Someone asks me first — do I add 嗎 to ask them back?
items.answer: No — use 呢. It sends the same question back. 嗎 would start a brand-new question.

right.pinyin: Wǒ shì Táiwān rén, nǐ ne?
right.english: I am Taiwanese. How about you?

words.meaning: how about; ending word that returns the question

items.question: Can I end a brand-new question with 呢?
items.answer: No. 呢 only repeats a question that was just asked. A new yes/no question ends with 嗎.

right.english: Do you like Taiwan?

items.question: My friend just said their name. Do I say the whole question again to ask them back?
items.answer: No. 呢 already points back to the question just asked. Add 呢 after the person and stop.

right.english: My name is Youmei. How about you?

words.meaning: how about; ending word that returns the question

text.traditional: A：我是日本人，你呢？ B：我是臺灣人。
text.simplified: A：我是日本人，你呢？ B：我是台湾人。
text.pinyin: A: Wǒ shì Rìběn rén, nǐ ne? B: Wǒ shì Táiwān rén.
text.english: A: I am Japanese. How about you? B: I am Taiwanese.

words.meaning: how about; ending word that returns the question

text.traditional: A：小林小姐叫友美，李先生呢？ B：他叫中明。
text.pinyin: A: Xiǎolín xiǎojiě jiào Yǒuměi, Lǐ xiānsheng ne? B: Tā jiào Zhōngmíng.
text.english: A: Miss Kobayashi is called Youmei. How about Mr. Li? B: He is called Zhongming.

words.meaning: how about; ending word that returns the question

text.traditional: A：王太太很累，王先生呢？ B：他不累。
text.simplified: A：王太太很累，王先生呢？ B：他不累。

text.english: A: Mrs. Wang is tired. How about Mr. Wang? B: He is not tired.

words.meaning: very; strengthens the word after it
how about; ending word that returns the question

grammarPages.titleTraditional: 主語 + 動詞 + 受詞
grammarPages.titleEnglish: Subject–Verb–Object Structure
grammarPages.learnerPromise: Build a complete sentence with a subject, a verb, and an object, in that order.
grammarPages.explanation: A Chinese sentence follows one order: Subject → Verb → Object. Put the subject first, then the verb, then the object. The object is the person or thing the verb affects.

teachingGlossary.meaning: not; goes right before the verb
to like; the verb in this sentence pattern
“to be”; links someone to an identity. Do not put it before a verb

grammarPages.pattern: S + (Neg)V + O

discoveryLab.title: Let the sentence grow one meaning block at a time
discoveryLab.description: Chinese listeners build the message in the same order that they hear it. Each step answers one more question.

choices.label: 1 · Subject
choices.english: I…
choices.note: The subject comes first. The listener knows who the sentence is about, but still waits for the verb.

choices.label: 2 · Verb
choices.english: I like…
choices.note: The verb comes second. The listener still needs the object — the person or thing that is liked.

choices.label: 3 · Object
choices.english: I like Taiwan.
choices.note: 臺灣 is the object. Subject → Verb → Object completes the sentence.

choices.label: Repair · no 是
choices.traditional: 我是喜歡臺灣。 → 我喜歡臺灣。
choices.simplified: 我是喜欢台湾。 → 我喜欢台湾。
choices.pinyin: Wǒ shì xǐhuān Táiwān. → Wǒ xǐhuān Táiwān.
choices.english: Repair it: I like Taiwan.
choices.note: 喜歡 is already the verb. Do not add 是 before it.

discoveryLab.takeaway: Build the sentence in order: Subject → Verb → Object. Put 不 right before the verb to make it negative.

sentenceSpine.title: Now switch the meaning without rebuilding the sentence
sentenceSpine.description: Keep the three slots in place and attach 不 directly to the verb.
notes: 不 stays right before the verb: 不喜歡.
Verbs like 喜歡 and 愛 do not need 是.

patternRows.english: I (don't) like him.

items.question: In English I say “I am liking Taiwan.” Do I need 是?
items.answer: No. 喜歡 already carries the feeling — it never takes 是. Keep 是 for names and identities, like 我是日本人.

right.english: I like Taiwan.

items.question: Where does 不 go to say I do not like something?
items.answer: Right before the verb: 不喜歡. Never after the verb or before the object.

right.english: I do not like Miss Wang.

items.question: Can the person or thing come first, like “Dad and Mom I love”?
items.answer: No. Chinese keeps the order Subject → Verb → Object. The object goes last.

right.english: I love Dad and Mom.

examples.teachingNote: The second part does not repeat 我.

text.traditional: 我喜歡李小姐，不喜歡王小姐。
text.simplified: 我喜欢李小姐，不喜欢王小姐。
text.pinyin: Wǒ xǐhuān Lǐ xiǎojiě, bù xǐhuān Wáng xiǎojiě.
text.english: I like Miss Li, but I do not like Miss Wang.

examples.teachingNote: 什麼 stands in for the thing you like.

text.traditional: 你喜歡什麼？
text.simplified: 你喜欢什么？
text.pinyin: Nǐ xǐhuān shénme?
text.english: What do you like?

examples.teachingNote: One verb can take two objects.

text.traditional: 我愛爸爸、媽媽。
text.simplified: 我爱爸爸、妈妈。
text.pinyin: Wǒ ài bàba, māma.
text.english: I love Dad and Mom.

items.question: Where does 不 go with 愛喝?
items.answer: 不 goes before the wanting word, not the action: 不愛喝, never 愛不喝.

items.question: Why can’t I add 嗎 to 忙不忙?
items.answer: The pair 忙不忙 already makes the question. Adding 嗎 gives it two question marks.

items.question: Why is it 有沒有, not 有不有?
items.answer: 有 takes 沒有 as its negative, so the pair repeats 有 and 沒有. Never pair 有 with 不.

grammarPages.titleTraditional: 數字 + 量詞 + 名詞
grammarPages.titleEnglish: Count Things with Measure Words
grammarPages.learnerPromise: Ask for and say how many people, books, flowers, or gifts there are.
grammarPages.explanation: Chinese needs a measure word between a number and noun: 個 for general nouns, 本 for books, and 朵 for flowers. Before a measure word, say 兩 for “two,” not 二.

teachingGlossary.meaning: connects a describing word or owner to a thing
how about it; okay or not
what about; asks the question back

grammarPages.pattern: Number or 幾 + measure word + noun

discoveryLab.title: Pick the right measure word
discoveryLab.description: The measure word links the number to the thing. The thing you name chooses the measure word.

choices.label: Books · 本
choices.english: two books
choices.note: Use 本 for books and similar things.

choices.label: Flowers · 朵
choices.english: how many flowers?
choices.note: 朵 counts flowers. 幾 still needs a measure word.

choices.label: General · 個
choices.english: one cake
choices.note: 個 is the useful general measure word in this lesson.

choices.label: Repair “two”
choices.pinyin: èr běn shū → liǎng běn shū
choices.english: two books
choices.note: Use 兩 before a measure word when counting two things.

discoveryLab.takeaway: Put them in order: number + measure word + thing: 兩 + 本 + 書.

two books

items.question: Do I need a word between the number and the thing?
items.answer: Yes — a measure word. Number and thing never sit side by side.

right.english: I buy three cakes.

items.question: Why do I say 兩 for "two" here, not 二?
items.answer: Before a measure word, two becomes 兩. 二 is only for plain counting, like 一二三.

right.english: I have two books.

items.question: Can I count everything with 個?
items.answer: No. 個 is the general one, but books take 本 and flowers take 朵.

grammarPages.titleEnglish: Say Who Receives the Gift
grammarPages.learnerPromise: Say who gives what gift to whom.
grammarPages.explanation: After 送, say the receiver first and the gift second: 送 + person + gift. Unlike English, Chinese adds no “to” before the receiver.

teachingGlossary.meaning: connects a describing word or owner to a thing
how about it; okay or not
what about; asks the question back

items.question: Do I say the gift first or the person first after 送?

grammarPages.titleTraditional: 這／那／哪 + 數量 + 名詞
grammarPages.titleEnglish: Point to This, That, or Which Thing
grammarPages.learnerPromise: Point to things that are near or far, or ask which one someone means.
grammarPages.explanation: Start with 這, 那, or 哪, then add the number, measure word, and noun. With one item, 一 is often omitted; with two, use 兩.

teachingGlossary.meaning: connects a describing word to a thing; can stand for a known thing
ending word for a yes-or-no question
how is it; what do you think

grammarPages.pattern: 這 / 那 / 哪 + number + measure word + noun

discoveryLab.title: Pick the pointing word first
discoveryLab.description: The first word shows distance or asks the listener to choose.
discoveryLab.prompt: What job should the first word do?

choices.label: Near · 這
choices.english: this kind of pen
choices.note: Use 這 for something near the speaker. 一 is normally omitted here.

choices.label: Far · 那
choices.english: those two books
choices.note: Use 那 for items farther away. Two becomes 兩 before 本.

choices.label: Choose · 哪
choices.english: which ten people?
choices.note: 哪 asks the listener to choose one.

discoveryLab.takeaway: Choose 這, 那, or 哪 first, then the full number + measure word + noun.

patternRows.english: this kind of pen
those two books
which ten people?

items.question: This book is in my hand. Do I point with 這 or 那?
items.answer: 這 — it is near you. 那 is for things farther away.

right.english: This book looks good.

items.question: I am choosing one thing to buy. Should my answer use 哪?
items.answer: No. 哪 asks "which?" in the question. Your answer chooses with 這 or 那.

right.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng mǎi zhè zhǒng bǐ.
right.english: I would like to buy this kind of pen.

items.question: Which comes first — the pointing word or the number?
items.answer: The pointing word first: 這 / 那 / 哪, then the number, measure word, and noun.

items.question: Where does 都 go in the sentence?
items.answer: Right after the whole group, before the action or describing word. Never at the start.

right.english: All of us like drinking tea.

items.question: How do I say "none of them likes tea" — 都不 or 不都?
items.answer: Put 都 before 不: 都不 means "every one does not". 不都 means "not all" — a different meaning.

right.english: None of them likes tea.

items.question: Can I use 都 with just one person, like "I all like this book"?
items.answer: No. 都 needs two or more people or things. With one, drop 都.

right.english: I like this book.

grammarPages.titleEnglish: Move the Thing into the Spotlight
grammarPages.learnerPromise: You can put the food, drink, gift, or thing you are talking about first.
grammarPages.explanation: Chinese can move a known thing to the front of the sentence. Pause, then say what the person does with it or how they feel about it. With several things up front, 都 means "all of them".

teachingGlossary.meaning: marks a new or strong situation
links a description or owner to a noun
how about it; okay or not
ending word that makes a yes-or-no question

grammarPages.pattern: Topic, Subject + (Neg) + Verb; plural topic, Subject + 都 + (Neg) + Verb

discoveryLab.title: Move the spotlight, keep the meaning
discoveryLab.description: The thing at the start tells the listener what this sentence is about. What follows is what you think or do about it.

choices.label: One thing
choices.english: Cake, I like.
choices.note: 蛋糕 is in the spotlight. 我喜歡 says what you think about it.

choices.label: Several things
choices.english: Books and pens, I have both.
choices.note: Two things come first, so 都 means "both".

choices.label: Contrast two things
choices.traditional: 茶，我喜歡；咖啡，我不喜歡。
choices.simplified: 茶，我喜欢；咖啡，我不喜欢。
choices.pinyin: Chá, wǒ xǐhuān; kāfēi, wǒ bù xǐhuān.
choices.english: Tea, I like; coffee, I do not.
choices.note: Putting each drink at the start makes the contrast easy to hear.

choices.label: Repair the pause
choices.traditional: 我蛋糕喜歡 → 蛋糕，我喜歡
choices.simplified: 我蛋糕喜欢 → 蛋糕，我喜欢
choices.pinyin: Wǒ dàngāo xǐhuān → dàngāo, wǒ xǐhuān
choices.english: Cake, I like.
choices.note: If you move a thing to the start, put it before the person and hear a small pause.

discoveryLab.takeaway: Put the thing first, pause, then say what you think or do.

items.question: When the thing goes first, do I need a pause?
items.answer: Yes — say the thing, pause, then the person and their feeling. In writing, that pause is a comma.

right.english: This pencil, I want it.

items.question: One thing up front — can I use 都?
items.answer: No. 都 means "all", so it needs two or more things. With one thing, just say 我喜歡.

right.english: Cake, I like.

items.question: I do not like coffee or tea. Where does 不 go?
items.answer: After 都: 都不喜歡. 都 + 不 means you feel this way about none of them.

right.english: Tea and coffee, I do not like either.

text.traditional: 茶，我喜歡；咖啡，我不喜歡。
text.simplified: 茶，我喜欢；咖啡，我不喜欢。
text.pinyin: Chá, wǒ xǐhuān; kāfēi, wǒ bù xǐhuān.
text.english: Tea, I like; coffee, I do not like.

text.english: This pencil, I want; that pencil, I do not want.

grammarPages.titleEnglish: Build Large Numbers by Place Value
grammarPages.learnerPromise: Read prices, quantities, and large numbers without guessing.
grammarPages.explanation: Chinese numbers are built from four words: 十 (10), 百 (100), 千 (1,000), 萬 (10,000). Read the biggest part first, then read what is left. When a place is skipped, say 零 once; in prices, the last place word is often dropped.

subsections.title: The four building blocks
subsections.explanation: These four words are the blocks. Put a number in front of a block to count it: 三 + 百 = 三百.

subsections.title: Read the first part, then the rest
subsections.explanation: Read the biggest part, then read what is left: 一百 + 一十五. When a place is skipped, the second part starts with 零: 一百 + 零五.

subsections.title: The last word can be dropped
subsections.explanation: In prices and amounts, the last place word is often left out. Both ways mean the same number: 八百五十 = 八百五.

subsections.title: Big numbers: how many 萬
subsections.explanation: 萬 counts ten-thousands. Say how many 萬, then add what is left: 七 萬 八千 is 7 × 10,000 + 8,000.

grammarPages.learnerPromise: Say “over ten,” “over one hundred,” or “a little after twelve” without claiming an exact number.

grammarPages.titleEnglish: Switch On a Learned Skill
grammarPages.learnerPromise: Say what someone knows—or does not know—how to do.
grammarPages.explanation: Use 會 before a learned or practiced skill. Put 不 before 會 for a missing skill. Here, 會 means “know how to”, not a future prediction.

ending word for a friendly reply
shows belonging or links a describing word

grammarPages.pattern: Subject +（Neg）會 + verb

items.question: I learned to swim. Do I say 我可以游泳 or 我會游泳?
items.answer: Use 會 — it reports a learned skill. 可以 talks about being allowed or a good option.

items.question: I know how to cook. Is it 我做飯會?
items.answer: No — 會 goes before the action word: 會做飯.

items.question: To say I cannot speak Chinese, is it 我會不說中文?
items.answer: No — 不 goes directly before 會: 不會說中文.

grammarPages.titleEnglish: Attach a Performance Meter
grammarPages.learnerPromise: Describe how well, fast, slowly, much, or happily an action is done.
grammarPages.explanation: 得 joins an action to a report about it, like 跑得很快. Keep the action word right before 得. For a two-part activity like 跑步 or 打網球, repeat the action word (跑步跑得很快) or move the thing forward (網球打得很好), so the action word still touches 得.

grammarPages.pattern: Subject + Verb + 得 + Adjective

discoveryLab.title: Choose the lane to 得
discoveryLab.description: Every lane ends with verb + 得 + performance. The activity’s shape decides what comes before it.

choices.label: Simple verb
choices.english: He runs very fast.

choices.label: Move object forward

choices.english: He plays tennis very well.
choices.note: 網球 becomes the topic, leaving 打 next to 得.

choices.label: Owned activity
choices.pinyin: Tā de wǎngqiú dǎ de hěn hǎo.
choices.english: His tennis playing is very good.
choices.note: 他的網球 is the topic; 打 still stands directly before 得.

choices.label: Repair the meter
choices.traditional: 他打得網球很好 → 他網球打得很好
choices.simplified: 他打得网球很好 → 他网球打得很好
choices.pinyin: Tā dǎ de wǎngqiú hěn hǎo → Tā wǎngqiú dǎ de hěn hǎo
choices.english: He plays tennis very well.
choices.note: Do not put 網球 after 得.

discoveryLab.takeaway: Protect the core: action word + 得 + performance. Move or repeat the thing when needed.

sentenceSpine.title: Build the unbreakable core
sentenceSpine.description: Three blocks. The middle block is the rule that never changes.
sentenceSpine.positiveEnglish: As for running, it is done very fast.
notes: Right: 跑步 + 跑得 + 很快. Repeat 跑 so the action word touches 得.
Wrong: 跑步 + 得 + 很快. The word 步 cannot attach directly to 得.

items.question: When I say he runs fast, is the middle word 的 or 得?
items.answer: 得. 得 links the action word to how it is done; 的 shows belonging.

grammarPages.titleEnglish: Turn the Warning Dial Slightly
grammarPages.learnerPromise: Describe a small, often inconvenient degree: a little tired, cold, or small.
grammarPages.explanation: Put 有一點兒 or 有點兒 right before a describing word to mean “a little.” It often softens a problem or an unwanted feeling. Do not add 很 after it.

grammarPages.pattern: Subject + 有（一）點（兒） + adjective

discoveryLab.title: Turn up only one notch
discoveryLab.description: The dial makes the describing word softer — often before you explain a problem or say no.
discoveryLab.prompt: What kind of small problem appears?

choices.label: Feeling
choices.english: I am a little tired.
choices.note: A mild feeling explains why rest may help.

choices.label: Evaluation
choices.english: The coffee is a little expensive.
choices.note: It is a little expensive, so you may choose another place.

choices.label: Reservation
choices.english: The clothes are a little small.
choices.note: The clothes look nice, but they are a little small.

choices.label: Repair order
choices.traditional: 我累有點兒 → 我有點兒累
choices.simplified: 我累有点儿 → 我有点儿累
choices.pinyin: Wǒ lèi yǒudiǎnr → Wǒ yǒudiǎnr lèi
choices.english: I am a little tired.
choices.note: Put 有點兒 before the describing word.

discoveryLab.takeaway: Say who or what first, then 有點兒, then the describing word. One small notch, often for a mild problem.

contrast.title: A little vs. a little amount
contrast.description: 有點兒 softens a describing word. 點兒 after an action or a thing means a small amount.

items.label: Small degree
items.note: 有點兒 comes right before the describing word 渴.

items.label: Small amount
items.english: I want to drink a little beverage.
items.note: 點兒 measures a small amount of 飲料.

patternRows.english: The weather is a little cold.
I am a little hungry.
This room is a little small.

items.question: This room is a little small. Do I need 是?
items.answer: No — 是 introduces who or what something is, not how it feels. Use 有一點兒 + 小.

right.pinyin: Zhè jiān fángjiān yǒu yìdiǎnr xiǎo.
right.english: This room is a little small.

items.question: Can I say 我有一點兒很累 to mean “very tired”?
items.answer: No — 有點兒 already does the degree job. It means “a little”, not “very”, so do not add 很.

right.english: I am a little tired.

items.question: The weather is a little cold. Is it 天氣冷有點兒?
items.answer: No — 有點兒 goes right before the describing word: 有點兒冷。

right.english: The weather is a little cold.

grammarPages.titleEnglish: Read the Green Light
grammarPages.learnerPromise: Offer a possible solution or ask whether an action is permitted.
grammarPages.explanation: 可以 can suggest a possible solution or give permission. Ask with 可以…嗎 or 可不可以; answer permission questions with 可以 or 不可以.

grammarPages.pattern: Subject + 可以 + Verb; Subject + 可以 + Verb 嗎？

discoveryLab.title: Read the green-light card
discoveryLab.description: The same 可以 either opens a possible path or checks permission.
discoveryLab.prompt: What job is 可以 doing?

choices.label: Suggestion
choices.english: You could drink hot tea.
choices.note: A problem comes first; 可以 offers one useful option.

choices.label: Ask permission
choices.english: May I go to the restroom?
choices.note: The speaker asks whether the action has a green light.

choices.label: No permission
choices.traditional: 不可以在捷運上吃東西。
choices.simplified: 不可以在捷运上吃东西。
choices.pinyin: Bù kěyǐ zài jiéyùn shàng chī dōngxi.
choices.english: Eating on the metro is not allowed.
choices.note: 不可以 removes permission.

choices.label: Repair order
choices.traditional: 我去可以嗎 → 我可以去嗎
choices.simplified: 我去可以吗 → 我可以去吗
choices.pinyin: Wǒ qù kěyǐ ma → Wǒ kěyǐ qù ma
choices.english: May I go?
choices.note: Put 可以 before the action.

discoveryLab.takeaway: Problem + 可以 = possible solution. 可以…嗎 = permission check.

contrast.title: Skill 會 vs. green-light 可以
contrast.description: Both can translate as “can,” but they answer different questions.

items.label: Permission
items.note: 可以 asks whether swimming is allowed.

items.question: May I go to the restroom? Can I say 去洗手間可以嗎?
items.answer: No — 可以 goes before the action word: 我可以去洗手間嗎？

right.english: May I go to the restroom?

items.question: To ask Mom if I may have ice cream, can I say 我想吃冰淇淋嗎?
items.answer: No — 想 means want. To ask permission, use 可以: 我可以吃冰淇淋嗎？

right.english: May I eat ice cream?

items.question: Do I add 嗎 after 可不可以, like 可以不可以去嗎?
items.answer: No — 可不可以 is already a question. Adding 嗎 doubles the question ending.

right.pinyin: Wǒmen kěyǐ qù kàn diànyǐng ma?

items.title: Grammar 1–3 · Routes and changing situations

grammarPages.lessonTitleEnglish: How Do We Get to the Hotel?
grammarPages.titleEnglish: Draw a Route with 從 and 到
grammarPages.learnerPromise: Say where a trip starts, where it ends, and why someone travels.
grammarPages.explanation: 從 is the start pin. 到 is the destination pin. Put each place right after its pin. Finish with 來 or 去. You can add the purpose (the why) at the end.

teachingGlossary.meaning: do not have; there is not

grammarPages.pattern: Person + 從 + start + 到 + destination + 來/去 + purpose

patternRows.english: Go from school to the drink shop to buy something.
Come from the hotel to my home to eat.
Come from Korea to Taiwan to visit a friend.

items.question: I want to say "I go from home to school." Which place comes right after 從?
items.answer: The start — the place you leave. 從 + start, 到 + destination: 我從家到學校去.

right.pinyin: Wǒ cóng jiā dào xuéxiào qù.
right.english: I go from home to school.

items.question: My friend is at the hotel and I am at home. She is coming to my place — 來 or 去?
items.answer: 來. Use 來 when the trip ends where you are; 去 points away from you. Her trip ends at my home, so: 她從飯店到家來.

right.pinyin: Tā cóng fàndiàn dào jiā lái.
right.english: She comes from the hotel to my home.

items.question: English says "go to school." Why is 我去到學校 not right in Chinese?
items.answer: Because 去 already means go, and 到 points at the destination. Chinese puts the place between them: 我到學校去.

right.english: I go to school.

routeLab.title: Move the route pins
routeLab.description: Read each trip left to right. Start, destination, direction, then purpose.

choices.label: Go to class

choices.note: The purpose 寄信 comes after the complete route.

choices.label: Visit a friend

choices.simplified: 她从韩国到台湾来看朋友。
choices.pinyin: Tā cóng Hánguó dào Táiwān lái kàn péngyǒu.
choices.english: She comes from Korea to Taiwan to visit a friend.
choices.note: Use 來 because the trip moves toward the speaker’s viewpoint.

routeLab.takeaway: Pins stay paired: 從 + start, 到 + destination. 來/去 shows which way the trip points, not the vehicle.

text.simplified: 我们从学校到超市去买东西。

grammarPages.lessonTitleEnglish: How Do We Get to the Hotel?
grammarPages.titleEnglish: Choose How the Trip Moves
grammarPages.learnerPromise: Ask how someone travels and answer with transport or walking.
grammarPages.explanation: Ask with 怎麼. Answer with one travel block before 來 or 去: 坐 + vehicle, 騎腳踏車, or 走路. Add 到 + place for the destination.

teachingGlossary.meaning: do not have; there is not

grammarPages.pattern: Person + travel method + 到 + place + 來/去

patternRows.english: I go to school by MRT.
We walk to the post office.
She comes to the hotel by taxi.

items.question: Can you 坐走路 to say you walk somewhere?
items.answer: No. 坐 is only for vehicles: 坐公車, 坐捷運, 坐計程車. Walking is its own travel block — just 走路, no 坐.

right.english: We walk there.

items.question: A friend asks 你怎麼去？ Do I answer 我去坐公車 or 我坐公車去?
items.answer: 我坐公車去 — the travel method comes before 去. 我去坐公車 means you are going somewhere to catch the bus.

right.english: I go by bus.

items.question: How do I ask "How are you going?" — 你為什麼去 or 你怎麼去?
items.answer: 你怎麼去. 怎麼 asks how; 為什麼 asks why, so it fits a reason, not a route.

right.english: How are you going?

routeLab.title: Swap the vehicle, keep the route
routeLab.description: Only the How block changes. Destination and direction stay stable.

choices.label: Fast MRT
choices.pinyin: Wǒmen zuò jiéyùn dào fàndiàn qù.
choices.english: We take the MRT to the hotel.

choices.label: Nearby walk
choices.english: We walk to the post office.
choices.note: 走路 works as a complete travel-method block; do not add 坐.

choices.label: Taxi to airport

choices.simplified: 我们坐计程车到机场去。
choices.pinyin: Wǒmen zuò jìchéngchē dào jīchǎng qù.
choices.english: We take a taxi to the airport.
choices.note: Transport comes before 到 + destination.

routeLab.takeaway: Ask 怎麼去？ Answer with one How block + 到 + destination + 去.

text.simplified: A：你们怎么去？ B：我们坐公车去。

text.simplified: A：饭店远不远？ B：不远，我们走路去。

grammarPages.lessonTitleEnglish: How Do We Get to the Hotel?
grammarPages.titleEnglish: Notice What Changed
grammarPages.learnerPromise: Put 了 at the end when a new situation becomes true.
grammarPages.explanation: Put 了 at the end of the sentence when something new happens. Before, it was not true; now it is. 了 can come after a feeling, a time, an arrival, or a new chance to act. 了 does not mean "past time".

teachingGlossary.meaning: do not have; there is not

grammarPages.pattern: New situation + 了

patternRows.english: I have become tired.
It is ten o’clock now.
The bus is here; we can board now.

items.question: Your stomach just started growling. Which tells people "I have become hungry"?
items.answer: 我餓了. 了 says the hungry state is new; 我很餓 only describes how hungry you are.

right.english: I am hungry now.

items.question: The bus is here and we can board. Where does 了 go in 我們可以上車?
items.answer: At the very end: 我們可以上車了. 了 closes the whole new situation — not between 可以 and 上車.

right.english: We can board the bus now.

items.question: Someone asks if you are tired now, after the long walk. Do you answer 我昨天累了?
items.answer: No — that says you were tired yesterday. Say 我現在累了: 了 marks the change, and the time word tells when.

right.english: I am tired now.

discoveryLab.title: Ring the change bell
discoveryLab.description: See the moment when a state becomes true for the first time.

choices.label: Hungry now
choices.english: I’m hungry now.
choices.note: The speaker was not hungry before; that state has changed.

choices.label: Bus arrived
choices.english: The bus is here now.
choices.note: The arrival creates a new situation.

choices.label: Time changed
choices.english: It’s ten now.
choices.note: The clock has reached a new reference point.

choices.label: Repair meaning
choices.traditional: 昨天我累了 → 我現在累了

choices.pinyin: Zuótiān wǒ lèi le → Wǒ xiànzài lèi le
choices.english: I am tired now.
choices.note: For this target meaning, make the changed situation current and clear.

discoveryLab.takeaway: Use 了 when "now it is different" matters.

text.simplified: 我累了，不想走了。

text.simplified: 公车来了，我们可以上车了。

text.english: The bus is here; now we can board.

text.english: It’s ten now; let’s go home first.

text.pinyin: Tā kě le, xiǎng xiān mǎi yǐnliào.
text.english: She has become thirsty and wants to buy a drink first.

dialogue.title: 對話一 · Dialogue 1
dialogue.setting: 上課前商量明天去天美飯店 · Planning tomorrow’s trip to Tianmei Hotel before class

text.traditional: 元真，我們明天幾點去找妳的韓國朋友？
text.simplified: 元真，我们明天几点去找你的韩国朋友？
text.pinyin: Yuánzhēn, wǒmen míngtiān jǐ diǎn qù zhǎo nǐ de Hánguó péngyǒu?

text.traditional: 我們下午四點要到天美飯店，她在那裡等我們。
text.simplified: 我们下午四点要到天美饭店，她在那里等我们。

grammarPages.lessonTitleEnglish: How Do We Get to the Hotel?
grammarPages.titleEnglish: Say the Activity First
grammarPages.learnerPromise: Name an activity first, then comment on it.
grammarPages.explanation: In Chinese, you can say the activity first, then say what you think about it. Think: activity → your comment.

teachingGlossary.meaning: do not have; there is not

grammarPages.pattern: Activity + comment

patternRows.english: Taking the MRT is convenient.
Walking there is too slow.
I like both running and swimming.

items.question: In English I say "It’s convenient to take the MRT." Does Chinese copy that order?
items.answer: No. Say the activity first, then the comment: 坐捷運很方便. The activity is what you are talking about; the comment follows.

right.english: Taking the MRT is convenient.

items.question: Do I need 是 between the activity and the comment — 走路去是太慢了?
items.answer: No. Put the activity first and the describing word right after it: 走路去太慢了. 是 is not needed here.

right.english: Walking there is too slow.

items.question: I like running, swimming, and tennis. Where does 都 go?
items.answer: Right after the person, before the action: 我都喜歡. Never after the verb: 我喜歡都跑步 is wrong.

right.traditional: 跑步、游泳、打網球，我都喜歡。
right.simplified: 跑步、游泳、打网球，我都喜欢。
right.pinyin: Pǎobù, yóuyǒng, dǎ wǎngqiú, wǒ dōu xǐhuān.
right.english: Running, swimming, and tennis — I like them all.

discoveryLab.title: Put the activity on stage
discoveryLab.description: The first chunk is what we are talking about; the rest is the comment.

choices.label: MRT
choices.english: Taking the MRT is convenient.
choices.note: 坐捷運 is the activity topic; 很方便 is the comment.

choices.label: Walking

choices.note: 走路去 is evaluated as one complete activity.

choices.label: Three sports
choices.traditional: 跑步、游泳、打網球，我都喜歡。
choices.simplified: 跑步、游泳、打网球，我都喜欢。
choices.pinyin: Pǎobù, yóuyǒng, dǎ wǎngqiú, wǒ dōu xǐhuān.
choices.english: Running, swimming, and tennis—I like them all.
choices.note: Several activities can share one comment.

choices.label: Repair focus
choices.traditional: 很方便坐捷運 → 坐捷運很方便
choices.simplified: 很方便坐捷运 → 坐捷运很方便
choices.pinyin: Hěn fāngbiàn zuò jiéyùn → Zuò jiéyùn hěn fāngbiàn
choices.english: Taking the MRT is convenient.
choices.note: Put the activity before the comment.

discoveryLab.takeaway: Activity first, comment second. You do not need 是 between them.

text.simplified: 坐公车很便宜，可是有一点慢。
text.pinyin: Zuò gōngchē hěn piányi, kěshì yǒu yìdiǎn màn.

text.simplified: 走路去太慢了，我们坐捷运吧。
text.pinyin: Zǒulù qù tài màn le, wǒmen zuò jiéyùn ba.
text.english: Walking is too slow; let’s take the MRT.

text.traditional: 唱歌、跳舞，她都喜歡。
text.simplified: 唱歌、跳舞，她都喜欢。
text.pinyin: Chànggē, tiàowǔ, tā dōu xǐhuān.
text.english: Singing and dancing—she likes both.

text.traditional: 住在學校附近很方便。
text.simplified: 住在学校附近很方便。
text.pinyin: Zhù zài xuéxiào fùjìn hěn fāngbiàn.
text.english: Living near school is convenient.

grammarPages.lessonTitleEnglish: How Do We Get to the Hotel?
grammarPages.titleEnglish: Pair Two True Qualities
grammarPages.learnerPromise: Describe two qualities or abilities that are true at the same time.
grammarPages.explanation: Put 又 before each quality: 又快又方便. Both sides describe the same person or thing, and they match in shape. Use 又…又… for two qualities that are true at the same time — not for two things.

teachingGlossary.meaning: do not have; there is not

grammarPages.pattern: Person or thing + 又 + quality 1 + 又 + quality 2

patternRows.english: The MRT is both fast and convenient.
A taxi is both fast and comfortable.
She is both cute and pretty.

items.question: Do I need 又 twice for "fast and convenient"?
items.answer: Yes — one 又 for each quality: 又快又方便. Each quality gets its own 又.

right.english: The MRT is fast and convenient.

items.question: Can I say 附近又學校又店 for "there is a school and a shop nearby"?
items.answer: No. 又…又… pairs qualities, not places or things. For two places, use 有…也有…: 附近有學校，也有店.

right.pinyin: Fùjìn yǒu xuéxiào, yě yǒu diàn.
right.english: There is a school and a shop nearby.

items.question: Can I mix 又 and 也 — 公車又快也便宜?
items.answer: No. Pair both qualities with 又: 又快又便宜. 也 adds a separate point; it does not build the pair.

right.english: The bus is fast and cheap.

discoveryLab.title: Balance the two sides
discoveryLab.description: Each 又 opens one matching description. Both sides describe the same person or thing.

choices.label: Transit

choices.simplified: 台北的捷运又快又方便。

choices.note: 快 and 方便 are two matching qualities.

choices.simplified: 我同学的妹妹又可爱又漂亮。

choices.english: My classmate’s younger sister is cute and pretty.

choices.note: Both body states are true together.

choices.pinyin: Jiéyùn yòu kuài fāngbiàn → Jiéyùn yòu kuài yòu fāngbiàn
choices.english: The MRT is both fast and convenient.
choices.note: Give each quality its own 又.

discoveryLab.takeaway: One person or thing, two matching 又 blocks.

text.simplified: 这家饭店又便宜又舒服。
text.pinyin: Zhè jiā fàndiàn yòu piányi yòu shūfu.
text.english: This hotel is inexpensive and comfortable.

text.traditional: 坐計程車又快又方便，可是比較貴。
text.simplified: 坐计程车又快又方便，可是比较贵。
text.pinyin: Zuò jìchéngchē yòu kuài yòu fāngbiàn, kěshì bǐjiào guì.
text.english: Taking a taxi is fast and convenient, but more expensive.

text.traditional: 元真又會唱歌又會跳舞。
text.simplified: 元真又会唱歌又会跳舞。
text.pinyin: Yuánzhēn yòu huì chànggē yòu huì tiàowǔ.
text.english: Yuanzhen can both sing and dance.

text.simplified: 我现在又累又渴，想先休息。
text.pinyin: Wǒ xiànzài yòu lèi yòu kě, xiǎng xiān xiūxí.
text.english: I am tired and thirsty now and want to rest first.

dialogue.title: 對話二 · Dialogue 2
dialogue.setting: 看地圖決定怎麼去飯店 · Reading the map to decide how to get to the hotel

text.traditional: 友美，妳看，天美飯店在大學路。我現在知道怎麼走了。
text.simplified: 友美，你看，天美饭店在大学路。我现在知道怎么走了。
text.pinyin: Yǒuměi, nǐ kàn, Tiānměi Fàndiàn zài Dàxué Lù. Wǒ xiànzài zhīdào zěnme zǒu le.
text.english: Look, Youmei. Tianmei Hotel is on Daxue Road. Now I know how to get there.

text.traditional: （看地圖）啊！天美飯店在這裡！我知道這個地方，附近有郵局跟超級市場。
text.simplified: （看地图）啊！天美饭店在这里！我知道这个地方，附近有邮局跟超级市场。
text.pinyin: (Kàn dìtú) A! Tiānměi Fàndiàn zài zhèlǐ! Wǒ zhīdào zhè ge dìfang, fùjìn yǒu yóujú gēn chāojíshìchǎng.
text.english: (Looking at the map) Ah! So here is Tianmei Hotel! I know this place. There is a post office and a supermarket nearby.

text.traditional: 我想走路去一定沒問題。
text.simplified: 我想走路去一定没问题。
text.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng zǒulù qù yídìng méi wèntí.
text.english: I think it will certainly be okay going there on foot.

text.traditional: 可是我覺得那裡有點兒遠，走路去太累了。
text.simplified: 可是我觉得那里有点儿远，走路去太累了。
text.pinyin: Kěshì wǒ juéde nàlǐ yǒudiǎnr yuǎn, zǒulù qù tài lèi le.
text.english: But I think it’s a bit far. It’s too tiring to get there on foot.

text.traditional: 妳想怎麼去？
text.simplified: 你想怎么去？
text.pinyin: Nǐ xiǎng zěnme qù?
text.english: How do you want to get there?

text.traditional: 坐捷運又方便又舒服，我們可以坐捷運。
text.simplified: 坐捷运又方便又舒服，我们可以坐捷运。
text.pinyin: Zuò jiéyùn yòu fāngbiàn yòu shūfu, wǒmen kěyǐ zuò jiéyùn.
text.english: Taking the MRT is convenient and comfortable. We can take the MRT.

text.traditional: 好，我們明天坐捷運去吧。
text.simplified: 好，我们明天坐捷运去吧。
text.pinyin: Hǎo, wǒmen míngtiān zuò jiéyùn qù ba.
text.english: Ok, let’s take the MRT to get there tomorrow.

grammarPages.titleEnglish: Rate the Experience with 好 and 難
grammarPages.learnerPromise: Use 好 and 難 with perception verbs for sensory quality and with action verbs for ease or difficulty.
grammarPages.explanation: Attach 好 or 難 to action words: 好 makes them pleasant or easy; 難 makes them unpleasant or difficult.

teachingGlossary.meaning: measure word for long thin things
good; easy or pleasant before an action word
difficult or unpleasant before an action word
ending word to check a guess
ending word for a yes/no question

subject.meaning: good; easy or pleasant before an action word

items.question: How do you say the skirt looks beautiful — 好看 or 看得好?
items.answer: 好看. 好 goes right before 看 and rates the skirt. 看得好 says a person sees or reads well, not how the thing looks.

right.english: This skirt looks beautiful.

words.meaning: measure word for long thin things

items.question: How do you say "English is hard to learn"? Where does 難 go?
items.answer: Put 難 right before the action word: 難學. The action word comes last, so 學難 is backwards.

right.english: English is hard to learn.

items.question: Why is 這裙子是很漂亮 not right?
items.answer: Describing-word sentences take no 是. Say the describing word right after the thing: 這條裙子很漂亮.

right.english: This skirt is beautiful.

words.meaning: measure word for long thin things

discoveryLab.title: Turn the experience dial
discoveryLab.description: The same two words can talk about how something feels or how hard it is to do.

choices.label: Looks good

choices.label: Easy to find

grammarPages.titleEnglish: Connect a Reason to Its Result
grammarPages.learnerPromise: Explain why something happens without making the listener guess.
grammarPages.explanation: 因為 starts the reason. 所以 starts the result. Say the reason first, then the result. Quick speech may leave one out, but you can keep both.

items.question: English can start with "So". Can I start my sentence with 所以?
items.answer: No. 因為 starts the reason, and 所以 starts the result that comes after it. Say the reason first.

right.traditional: 因為好看，所以很多人買。
right.simplified: 因为好看，所以很多人买。
right.pinyin: Yīnwèi hǎokàn, suǒyǐ hěn duō rén mǎi.
right.english: Because it looks good, many people buy it.

items.question: My friend asks 你為什麼不想走？ How do I start the answer?
items.answer: Start with 因為 + the reason: 因為他很累. 所以 begins the result, not the answer to a why question.

right.english: Because he is tired.

items.question: The shoes are too small, so I will not buy them. Which part goes after 因為?
items.answer: The cause — the shoes being too small. 因為 starts the cause, and 所以 starts the result: I do not buy.

right.traditional: 因為鞋子太小，所以不買。
right.simplified: 因为鞋子太小，所以不买。
right.pinyin: Yīnwèi xiézi tài xiǎo, suǒyǐ bú mǎi.
right.english: Because the shoes are too small, I will not buy them.

sentenceSpine.title: Follow the logic bridge
sentenceSpine.description: Read the thought left to right: reason, connector, result.

subject.label: 因為 + cause

sentenceSpine.positiveEnglish: Because this brand is famous, many people buy it.
notes: 所以 points to the result that follows.
Do not swap the cause and the result to match English word order.

examples.teachingNote: 因為 states the cause, and 所以 gives the result in a conversational answer.

items.question: How do you say "try it on and see"? Where does 看 go?

items.question: Which word do you repeat to say "try drinking it"?
items.answer: The action word you are trying — here 喝: 喝喝看. Repeating 看 instead gives 看看喝, which is backwards.

items.question: Which time goes right after 從 — the start time or the finish time?
items.answer: The start time. 從 opens the start, and 到 opens the finish: 我從四點到五點半上英文課.

right.traditional: 我從四點到五點半上英文課。
right.simplified: 我从四点到五点半上英文课。
right.pinyin: Wǒ cóng sì diǎn dào wǔ diǎn bàn shàng Yīngwén kè.
right.english: I have English class from 4:00 to 5:30.

items.question: My class runs Monday to Friday. Do I need 從 — is 我星期一到星期五都有課 okay?
items.answer: Use both pins. 從 opens the start, and 到 opens the finish: 我從星期一到星期五都有課.

right.traditional: 我從星期一到星期五都有課。
right.simplified: 我从星期一到星期五都有课。
right.pinyin: Wǒ cóng xīngqí yī dào xīngqí wǔ dōu yǒu kè.
right.english: I have class from Monday to Friday.

items.question: I am busy from morning to night. Is 都 needed, and where does it go?
items.answer: Yes — 都 shows the whole range is covered. It goes right after the range: 我從早到晚都忙。

right.pinyin: Wǒ cóng zǎo dào wǎn dōu máng.
right.english: I am busy from morning to night.

grammarPages.pattern: Person + 先 + action 1，再 + action 2

patternRows.english: First play tennis, then swim.
First take the MRT, then take a bus.
First return to the dorm, then go find him.

items.question: Where does 先 go — before the first action or after it?
items.answer: Before it. 先 + first action, 再 + next action: 我先看書，再做功課.

right.pinyin: Wǒ xiān kànshū, zài zuò gōngkè.
right.english: I read first, then do homework.

items.question: I do both actions myself. Do I say 我 twice — 我做功課，我再去?
items.answer: No — one person doing both actions is named once: 我先做功課，再去。

right.pinyin: Wǒ xiān zuò gōngkè, zài qù.
right.english: First I do homework, then I go.

items.question: Second step: do I repeat the action word — 再坐公車 or 再公車?
items.answer: Repeat it. Each step keeps its own action word: 你要先坐捷運，再坐公車.

right.traditional: 你要先坐捷運，再坐公車。
right.simplified: 你要先坐捷运，再坐公车。

grammarPages.titleEnglish: Say When an Action Is Possible
grammarPages.learnerPromise: Use 能 to express physical capability, rules and permissions, and possibility due to objective factors.
grammarPages.explanation: Use 能 or 不能 to talk about what you can or cannot do: whether your body is able to do it, whether rules allow it, or whether your schedule makes it possible.

patternRows.english: He is injured; he cannot walk right now.

items.question: A friend asks 我能在這裡用電腦嗎？ Do I answer with 可以 or 能?
items.answer: 可以. Giving or asking permission uses 可以: 可以，沒問題。 能 is for ability, rules, or the situation.

right.english: Sure, no problem.

items.question: He hurt his leg and can only walk. Is it 能只走 or 只能走?
items.answer: 只能走. 只 comes before 能: 只能 + action means "can only do this one thing."

right.english: He can only walk now.

items.question: Phones are not allowed in class. Do I say 不能看手機 or 不可以看手機?
items.answer: 不能看手機. Each little helping word takes its own "not": 能 → 不能, 可以 → 不可以. A rule closes the action, so use 不能.

right.traditional: 上課時間我們不能看手機。
right.simplified: 上课时间我们不能看手机。
right.pinyin: Shàngkè shíjiān wǒmen bù néng kàn shǒujī.
right.english: We cannot look at phones during class.

items.question: To ask "Can I use that classroom?", do I say 我能不能用那間教室嗎 with 嗎?
items.answer: No — 能不能 already asks the question, so 嗎 is not needed. Use 能不能…, not 能不能…嗎.

right.pinyin: Wǒ néng bù néng yòng nà jiān jiàoshì?
right.english: Can I use that classroom?

subsections.title: Physical Ability (Can / Cannot Do)
subsections.explanation: Use 能 or 不能 for what your body is physically able to do, like birds being able to fly, or resting when you can’t run.

patternRows.english: He is injured; he cannot walk now.

subsections.title: Rules and Permission (Allowed / Not Allowed)
subsections.explanation: Use 不能 when rules or manners say you shouldn’t do something, like not eating on the MRT or not looking at phones during class.

patternRows.english: In the library, you cannot drink beverages.

subsections.title: Circumstances and Schedules (Possible / Not Possible)
subsections.explanation: Use 能 or 不能 when outside situations decide if you can make it, like having class so you can’t hang out, or being far away.

text.traditional: 太好了！在那裡看書很舒服。我們每天都能用那間教室嗎？
text.simplified: 太好了！在那里看书很舒服。我们每天都能用那间教室吗？
text.pinyin: Tài hǎo le! Zài nàlǐ kànshū hěn shūfu. Wǒmen měitiān dōu néng yòng nà jiān jiàoshì ma?
text.english: Great! Studying there is comfortable. Can we use that classroom every day?

words.meaning: ending word that shows a new situation
be in the middle of an action; at
very; links a thing to a quality
ending word that makes a yes-no question

text.traditional: 我們班只能禮拜一跟禮拜二下午用。
text.simplified: 我们班只能礼拜一跟礼拜二下午用。
text.pinyin: Wǒmen bān zhǐ néng lǐbài yī gēn lǐbài èr xiàwǔ yòng.

text.traditional: 可是這些時間我都有語言交換，不能去。
text.simplified: 可是这些时间我都有语言交换，不能去。
text.pinyin: Kěshì zhèxiē shíjiān wǒ dōu yǒu yǔyán jiāohuàn, bù néng qù.
text.english: But I have language exchange then, so I cannot go.

text.traditional: 別的時間可以嗎？
text.simplified: 别的时间可以吗？
text.pinyin: Biéde shíjiān kěyǐ ma?
text.english: Could you use another time?

words.meaning: ending word that makes a yes-no question

text.traditional: 我朋友最近比較忙，別的時間他沒有空。
text.simplified: 我朋友最近比较忙，别的时间他没有空。
text.pinyin: Wǒ péngyǒu zuìjìn bǐjiào máng, biéde shíjiān tā méi yǒukòng.
text.english: My friend is busier lately and is not free at other times.

words.meaning: relatively; more, with a known comparison

text.traditional: 我們去問老師，也許他可以幫你。
text.simplified: 我们去问老师，也许他可以帮你。
text.pinyin: Wǒmen qù wèn lǎoshī, yěxǔ tā kěyǐ bāng nǐ.
text.english: Let us ask the teacher. Maybe he can help.

text.traditional: 好，希望老師可以幫我。
text.simplified: 好，希望老师可以帮我。
text.pinyin: Hǎo, xīwàng lǎoshī kěyǐ bāng wǒ.
text.english: Okay. I hope the teacher can help me.

grammarPages.titleEnglish: Connect a Person to an Action with 跟
grammarPages.learnerPromise: Use 跟 to do things together with someone, to speak or request from someone, and to learn or borrow from someone.
grammarPages.explanation: 跟 connects you with another person. Use it to do things together (“with”), to talk or ask (“to”), or to learn or borrow (“from”).

lessonWorld.title: Send the right care message
lessonWorld.prompt: Yuanzhen needs to pass the teacher’s advice to Guoan.
lessonWorld.traditional: 老師要我跟國安說幾句話。
lessonWorld.simplified: 老师要我跟国安说几句话。
lessonWorld.pinyin: Lǎoshī yào wǒ gēn Guó’ān shuō jǐ jù huà.
lessonWorld.english: The teacher wants me to say a few things to Guoan.

teachingGlossary.meaning: links a description to a noun
ending word: a change or a finish

grammarPages.pattern: 和…一起 ｜ 對…說話／請假 ｜ 向…學習／借

patternRows.english: Tonight I will eat with a friend.
He speaks English with his family.
I learn calligraphy from Teacher Li.

items.question: I go to the hospital with my friend — where does 跟 go?
items.answer: Right before the person who joins you: 跟朋友. The person never comes before 跟.

right.english: I go to the hospital with my friend.

items.question: I tell my friend something — where does my friend go?
items.answer: The person you tell comes right after 跟, before the action word: 我跟朋友說。

right.english: I speak to my friend.

items.question: Can 和 do the same job as 跟?
items.answer: 和 lists two people as equals — “my friend and I”. 跟 connects the person to your action: go WITH, speak TO.

right.english: I speak Chinese with the doctor.

discoveryLab.title: Move 跟, move the connection
discoveryLab.description: The same people can join different parts of the event.

choices.label: Go together
choices.english: I go to the hospital with my friend.
choices.note: 跟朋友 goes with 去醫院: the friend joins the trip.

choices.label: Talk there
choices.pinyin: Wǒ qù yīyuàn gēn péngyǒu shuōhuà.
choices.english: I go to the hospital to speak with my friend.
choices.note: Here 跟朋友 goes with 說話, not the trip.

choices.label: Tell the teacher
choices.english: I first ask the teacher for leave.
choices.note: 老師 receives the request.

discoveryLab.takeaway: Read 跟 with the person and the action after it.

text.traditional: 今天晚上我要跟朋友吃飯。
text.simplified: 今天晚上我要跟朋友吃饭。
text.pinyin: Jīntiān wǎnshang wǒ yào gēn péngyǒu chīfàn.
text.english: Tonight I am going to eat dinner with a friend.

text.traditional: 我常常跟他一起去百貨公司買東西。
text.simplified: 我常常跟他一起去百货公司买东西。
text.pinyin: Wǒ chángcháng gēn tā yìqǐ qù bǎihuò gōngsī mǎi dōngxi.
text.english: I often go to the department store together with him to buy things.

text.traditional: 我喜歡跟家人去海邊玩。
text.simplified: 我喜欢跟家人去海边玩。
text.pinyin: Wǒ xǐhuān gēn jiārén qù hǎibiān wán.
text.english: I like going to the beach with my family.

text.traditional: 他跟家人說英文，跟同學說中文。
text.simplified: 他跟家人说英文，跟同学说中文。
text.pinyin: Tā gēn jiārén shuō Yīngwén, gēn tóngxué shuō Zhōngwén.
text.english: He speaks English to his family and Chinese to his classmates.

text.traditional: 計程車司機跟我說：「去機場 1,200 塊錢。」
text.simplified: 计程车司机跟我说：「去机场 1,200 块钱。」
text.pinyin: Jìchéngchē sījī gēn wǒ shuō: "Qù jīchǎng 1,200 kuài qián."
text.english: The taxi driver said to me: "Going to the airport is 1,200 dollars."

text.traditional: 我明天不能來上課，今天要先跟老師請假。
text.simplified: 我明天不能来上课，今天要先跟老师请假。
text.pinyin: Wǒ míngtiān bù néng lái shàngkè, jīntiān yào xiān gēn lǎoshī qǐngjià.
text.english: I cannot attend class tomorrow, so today I need to ask the teacher for leave first.

words.pinyin: wǒ míngtiān bù néng lái shàngkè
words.meaning: I cannot come to class tomorrow

examples.teachingNote: 跟...學 means to learn from someone.

text.traditional: 我跟沈老師學書法。
text.simplified: 我跟沈老师学书法。
text.pinyin: Wǒ gēn Shěn lǎoshī xué shūfǎ.
text.english: I learn calligraphy from Teacher Shen.

examples.teachingNote: 跟...要錢 means to ask for money from parents.

text.traditional: 他二十歲了，不跟爸媽要錢了。
text.simplified: 他二十岁了，不跟爸妈要钱了。
text.pinyin: Tā èrshí suì le, bù gēn bàmā yào qián le.
text.english: He is twenty years old; he no longer asks his parents for money.

examples.teachingNote: 跟...買舊車 means to buy a used car from a friend.

text.traditional: 我不想跟朋友買舊車，我想買新車。
text.simplified: 我不想跟朋友买旧车，我想买新车。
text.pinyin: Wǒ bù xiǎng gēn péngyǒu mǎi jiù chē, wǒ xiǎng mǎi xīn chē.
text.english: I don't want to buy a used car from a friend; I want to buy a new car.

questions.repairFeedback: Use 跟他一起.

questions.repairFeedback: Use 跟同學說中文.

subsections.title: Doing Things with Someone (With)
subsections.explanation: Put 跟 before the person you do an activity with, like “have dinner with friends” or “go shopping with him.”

patternRows.english: Tonight I will eat with a friend.

subsections.title: Talking to Someone (To)
subsections.explanation: Put 跟 before the person you are talking to, like “he speaks English to his family” or “asking the teacher for time off.”

patternRows.english: He speaks English with his family.

subsections.title: Learning or Getting from Someone (From)
subsections.explanation: Put 跟 before the person you learn or receive something from, like “learn calligraphy from Teacher Shen” or “borrow money from a friend.”

patternRows.english: I learn calligraphy from Teacher Li.

grammarPages.titleEnglish: Noun Modified by a Clause with 的
grammarPages.learnerPromise: Identify a person or thing by describing it first.
grammarPages.explanation: Put your description first, add 的, and then say the person or thing you mean: Description + 的 + Noun. If you want to point out someone specific, add “this” or “that” right after 的.

lessonWorld.title: Find the person who needs help
lessonWorld.prompt: Several people are waiting. Which person has a cold?
lessonWorld.traditional: 請找感冒的人。
lessonWorld.simplified: 请找感冒的人。
lessonWorld.pinyin: Qǐng zhǎo gǎnmào de rén.
lessonWorld.english: Find the person who has a cold.

teachingGlossary.meaning: links a description to a noun
ending word: a change or a finish

grammarPages.pattern: Description + 的 + noun

patternRows.english: The characters I wrote.
The person who has a cold.
That doctor wearing a mask.

items.question: The person who has a cold — which word comes last?
items.answer: The person. Put the description first, then 的, then the person: 感冒的人。

right.english: the person who has a cold

words.meaning: links a description to a noun

items.question: Do I always need 的 between the description and the person?
items.answer: Yes. 的 is the link: description + 的 + person. Without it, the words do not join into one label.

right.english: the doctor wearing a mask

words.meaning: links a description to a noun

items.question: The medicine the doctor gave — where does 的 go?
items.answer: Right after the action word, before the thing: 醫生給的藥。The whole description stays before 的.

right.english: the medicine the doctor gave

words.meaning: links a description to a noun

discoveryLab.title: Change the label, find someone new
discoveryLab.description: The noun stays last. Everything before 的 tells you which one.

choices.label: Has a cold
choices.english: the person who has a cold
choices.note: 感冒 identifies the person.

choices.label: Wears a mask
choices.english: the person wearing a mask
choices.note: The whole action 戴口罩 identifies the person.

choices.label: Mask-wearing doctor
choices.english: the doctor wearing a mask
choices.note: Changing the final noun changes who the label identifies.

choices.label: Repair the order
choices.traditional: 人感冒的 → 感冒的人
choices.simplified: 人感冒的 → 感冒的人
choices.pinyin: rén gǎnmào de → gǎnmào de rén
choices.english: Move the description before 的 and the noun.
choices.note: Chinese builds the label first, then names the noun.

discoveryLab.takeaway: Ask: “Which person or thing?” Put the answer before 的.

examples.teachingNote: The modifying clause 我寫 precedes the modified noun 字.

text.traditional: 我寫的字太小了，老師看不懂。
text.simplified: 我写的字太小了，老师看不懂。
text.pinyin: Wǒ xiě de zì tài xiǎo le, lǎoshī kànbudǒng.
text.english: The characters I wrote are too small; the teacher cannot read them.

examples.teachingNote: 他唱 modifies the noun 歌.

text.traditional: 他唱的歌很好聽，是哪國歌？
text.simplified: 他唱的歌很好听，是哪国歌？
text.pinyin: Tā chàng de gē hěn hǎotīng, shì nǎ guó gē?
text.english: The song he sings sounds very nice; which country's song is it?

examples.teachingNote: 他們說 modifies the noun 話.

text.traditional: 我不懂他們說的話，你懂嗎？
text.simplified: 我不懂他们说的话，你懂吗？
text.pinyin: Wǒ bù dǒng tāmen shuō de huà, nǐ dǒng ma?
text.english: I don't understand the words they are saying; do you understand?

examples.teachingNote: 在台北坐捷運 modifies 人 as a category of people.

text.traditional: 在台北坐捷運的人很多。
text.simplified: 在台北坐捷运的人很多。
text.pinyin: Zài Táiběi zuò jiéyùn de rén hěn duō.
text.english: People who take the MRT in Taipei are many.

examples.teachingNote: 會說中文 modifies 人.

text.traditional: 會說中文的人不一定會教中文。
text.simplified: 会说中文的人不一定会教中文。
text.pinyin: Huì shuō Zhōngwén de rén bù yídìng huì jiāo Zhōngwén.
text.english: People who can speak Chinese do not necessarily know how to teach Chinese.

examples.teachingNote: 常常生病 modifies 人.

text.traditional: 常常生病的人要注意身體健康。
text.simplified: 常常生病的人要注意身体健康。
text.pinyin: Chángcháng shēngbìng de rén yào zhùyì shēntǐ jiànkāng.
text.english: People who get sick often need to pay attention to their health.

examples.teachingNote: Clause 我太太買 precedes 的那件衣服 (Dem + M + N).

text.traditional: 我太太買的那件衣服好看。
text.simplified: 我太太买的那件衣服好看。
text.pinyin: Wǒ tàitai mǎi de nà jiàn yīfu hǎokàn.
text.english: That piece of clothing my wife bought looks good.

examples.teachingNote: Clause 你問 precedes 的這兩個問題 (Dem + Num + M + N).

text.traditional: 你問的這兩個問題都非常難。
text.simplified: 你问的这两个问题都非常难。
text.pinyin: Nǐ wèn de zhè liǎng ge wèntí dōu fēicháng nán.
text.english: These two questions that you asked are both extremely difficult.

examples.teachingNote: Clause 在跳舞 precedes 的那些學生.

text.traditional: 在跳舞的那些學生都是我的朋友。
text.simplified: 在跳舞的那些学生都是我的朋友。
text.pinyin: Zài tiàowǔ de nàxiē xuésheng dōu shì wǒ de péngyǒu.
text.english: Those students who are dancing are all my friends.

subsections.title: Describing Things and Ideas (Action + 的 + Noun)
subsections.explanation: Put what happened before 的 to describe a thing, like “the words I wrote” or “the apple Mom gave me.”

patternRows.english: The character I wrote.
The apple my mom gave me.

subsections.title: Describing People (Action + 的 + Person)
subsections.explanation: Describe someone’s action or habit before 的 to say what kind of person they are, like “people who have a cold” or “a child who can cook.”

patternRows.english: The person who has a cold.
The child who knows how to cook.
The old gentleman who exercises often.

subsections.title: Pointing to Specific People or Things (Description + 的 + This / That)
subsections.explanation: When pointing to one specific person or item, put words like “this” or “that” right after 的, like “that doctor wearing a mask.”

patternRows.english: That doctor wearing a mask.

grammarPages.titleTraditional: 把行動調多一點或少一點
grammarPages.titleEnglish: Do an Action More or Less
grammarPages.learnerPromise: Give useful advice with 多 or 少 before an action.
grammarPages.explanation: Put 多 or 少 before the action you want someone to increase or reduce.

lessonWorld.title: Adjust the advice
lessonWorld.prompt: Guoan needs more water and rest, but less phone time.
lessonWorld.traditional: 你應該多喝水、少看手機。
lessonWorld.simplified: 你应该多喝水、少看手机。
lessonWorld.pinyin: Nǐ yīnggāi duō hē shuǐ, shǎo kàn shǒujī.
lessonWorld.english: You should drink more water and look at your phone less.

teachingGlossary.meaning: links a description to a noun
ending word: a change or a finish

grammarPages.pattern: 多／少 + action

patternRows.english: drink more water
rest more
look at the phone less

items.question: Why can’t I just say 多水 for “more water”?
items.answer: 多 and 少 adjust an action word. Water is a thing, so add the action first: 多喝水。

right.english: Drink more water.

items.question: Does 多 come before or after the action?
items.answer: Before it: 多休息, 少看手機. Never after the action word.

right.english: Rest more.

items.question: How do I say “drink MORE water” as advice?
items.answer: 很多水 means “a lot of water”. For advice to drink more, put 多 right before the action: 多喝水。

right.english: You should drink more water.

discoveryLab.title: Turn the action up or down
discoveryLab.description: 多 and 少 change how often or how much the action happens.

choices.label: More water
choices.english: Drink more water.
choices.note: 多 sits before the action 喝.

choices.label: More rest
choices.english: Rest more.
choices.note: The advice increases the action.

choices.label: Less phone
choices.english: Look at your phone less.
choices.note: 少 reduces 看手機.

choices.label: Repair the advice
choices.english: Add the missing action.
choices.note: Water is a thing. Health advice needs the action 喝.

discoveryLab.takeaway: Choose an action first. Put 多 or 少 directly before it.

examples.teachingNote: One action goes up, one goes down.

text.traditional: 你應該多運動，少喝一點兒酒。
text.simplified: 你应该多运动，少喝一点儿酒。
text.pinyin: Nǐ yīnggāi duō yùndòng, shǎo hē yìdiǎnr jiǔ.
text.english: You should exercise more and drink a little less alcohol.

examples.teachingNote: Source health advice.

text.traditional: 我發燒了，醫生跟我說要多喝水、多休息、少看手機。
text.simplified: 我发烧了，医生跟我说要多喝水、多休息、少看手机。
text.pinyin: Wǒ fāshāo le, yīshēng gēn wǒ shuō yào duō hē shuǐ, duō xiūxi, shǎo kàn shǒujī.
text.english: I have a fever; the doctor told me to drink more water, rest more, and look at my phone less.

words.meaning: ending word: a change or a finish

examples.teachingNote: 多 changes 休息.

text.traditional: 生病的時候要多休息。
text.simplified: 生病的时候要多休息。
text.pinyin: Shēngbìng de shíhou yào duō xiūxi.
text.english: When sick, rest more.

words.meaning: links a description to a noun

examples.teachingNote: The pattern can repeat across several actions.

text.traditional: 我們學習語言，平常應該要多聽、多說、多寫、多練習。
text.simplified: 我们学习语言，平常应该要多听、多说、多写、多练习。
text.pinyin: Wǒmen xuéxí yǔyán, píngcháng yīnggāi yào duō tīng, duō shuō, duō xiě, duō liànxí.
text.english: When we learn a language, we should listen, speak, write, and practice more in daily life.

dialogue.title: 對話一 · Dialogue 1
dialogue.setting: 在學校 · At school

text.traditional: 老師，國安今天要請假。他發燒了，不能來上課。
text.simplified: 老师，国安今天要请假。他发烧了，不能来上课。
text.pinyin: Lǎoshī, Guó’ān jīntiān yào qǐngjià. Tā fāshāo le, bù néng lái shàngkè.
text.english: Teacher, Guoan has to take a leave today. He has a fever and he can’t come to school.

words.meaning: ending word: a change or a finish

text.traditional: 他發燒了？那他應該去看醫生。
text.simplified: 他发烧了？那他应该去看医生。
text.pinyin: Tā fāshāo le? Nà tā yīnggāi qù kàn yīshēng.
text.english: He has a fever? He should see a doctor then.

items.question: I will come tomorrow — where does 明天 go?

items.question: Does 會 mean “can” or “will”?

items.question: For “I will visit you tomorrow”, can I use 可以?

grammarPages.pattern: 如果／要是 + condition， 就 + result

patternRows.english: If you have a fever, then take medicine.

items.question: Where does 就 go in an if-then sentence?
items.answer: 就 starts the result, after the condition. It never sits inside the condition.

right.english: If you have a fever, then take medicine.

items.question: In the fever sentence, where does 了 go?
items.answer: 了 goes right after the action word that marks the change: 發燒了. At the very end it would change the sentence into a new decision, not a health instruction.

right.pinyin: Rúguǒ fāshāo le, jiù chī yào.
right.english: If you develop a fever, take medicine.

words.meaning: ending word: a change or a finish

items.question: Can I say the result first, like in English?
items.answer: No — the condition comes first, then 就 + the result: IF this, THEN that. 要是 works the same as 如果.

right.english: If you have a fever, then rest.

discoveryLab.title: Change the condition, change the result

items.title: Grammar 1–3 · Completed, unfinished, and focused past events

grammarPages.lessonTitleEnglish: How Did You Meet Each Other?
grammarPages.titleEnglish: Completed Action with 了
grammarPages.learnerPromise: Say that an action is finished.
grammarPages.explanation: Put 了 after the action word to show it is finished. When talking about amounts (like “two cups” or “ten pages”), a single 了 means you stopped there, while two 了’s mean you reached that amount so far and may keep going.

teachingGlossary.meaning: links an action word to how it was done

grammarPages.pattern: Verb + object or amount + 了

patternRows.english: I completed the homework.
I drank it.
Dad bought it.

items.question: Where does 了 go in “I wrote the homework yesterday”?
items.answer: Right after the action word. 了 follows 寫, before the homework.

right.english: I wrote the homework yesterday.

items.question: Do I need 了 for something I do every day?
items.answer: No. 了 marks one finished action. For a habit you repeat, leave 了 out.

right.english: I drink coffee every day.

items.question: How do I say “I am writing a card” right now?
items.answer: Use 在 before the action word. 了 would say the card is already done.

right.english: I am writing a card.

discoveryLab.title: Watch the action reach DONE
discoveryLab.description: The picture—not the English time words—shows whether the action is happening now or already finished.

choices.label: General action
choices.english: I do homework.
choices.note: The sentence names the activity. It does not say if it is happening now or finished.

choices.label: Happening now
choices.english: I am doing homework now.
choices.note: 在 shows the action is happening now.

choices.label: Completed
choices.english: I completed the homework.
choices.note: 了 shows the action is finished.

discoveryLab.takeaway: Ask: is the action general, happening now, or finished?

examples.teachingNote: Single 了 after V(O) indicates a completed action in the past.

text.traditional: 他已經去上課了。
text.simplified: 他已经去上课了。
text.pinyin: Tā yǐjīng qù shàngkè le.
text.english: He has already gone to class.

examples.teachingNote: 今天早上去看醫生了 indicates the visit is completed.

text.traditional: 我今天早上去看醫生了。
text.simplified: 我今天早上去看医生了。
text.pinyin: Wǒ jīntiān zǎoshang qù kàn yīshēng le.
text.english: I went to see the doctor this morning.

examples.teachingNote: 都寫功課了 confirms the homework is finished.

text.traditional: 我跟弟弟都寫功課了。
text.simplified: 我跟弟弟都写功课了。
text.pinyin: Wǒ gēn dìdi dōu xiě gōngkè le.
text.english: My younger brother and I have both finished our homework.

examples.teachingNote: Comparative pair: (a) Single 了 for past completed quantity; (b) Double 了 indicates so far, with more likely to come.

text.traditional: 我上個禮拜學了十個中國字。我已經學了四百多個中國字了。
text.simplified: 我上个礼拜学了十个中国字。我已经学了四百多个中国字了。
text.pinyin: Wǒ shàng ge lǐbài xué le shí ge Zhōngguózì. Wǒ yǐjīng xué le sìbǎi duō ge Zhōngguózì le.
text.english: I learned ten Chinese characters last week. I have already learned more than 400 Chinese characters so far.

examples.teachingNote: Comparative pair: (a) Single 了 for buying a car; (b) Double 了 indicates he already bought one and still wants another.

text.traditional: 爸爸上個月買了一輛新車。爸爸已經買了一輛新車了，還想再買一輛。
text.simplified: 爸爸上个月买了一辆新车。爸爸已经买了一辆新车了，还想再买一辆。
text.pinyin: Bàba shàng ge yuè mǎi le yí liàng xīn chē. Bàba yǐjīng mǎi le yí liàng xīn chē le, hái xiǎng zài mǎi yí liàng.
text.english: Dad bought a new car last month. Dad has already bought a new car, and he still wants to buy another one.

examples.teachingNote: Comparative pair: (a) Single 了 for eating two apples yesterday; (b) Double 了 indicates he ate one so far and wants more.

text.traditional: 他昨天晚上吃了兩個蘋果。他很愛吃蘋果，已經吃了一個了，還想再吃。
text.simplified: 他昨天晚上吃了两个苹果。他很爱吃苹果，已经吃了一个了，还想再吃。
text.pinyin: Tā zuótiān wǎnshang chī le liǎng ge píngguǒ. Tā hěn ài chī píngguǒ, yǐjīng chī le yí ge le, hái xiǎng zài chī.
text.english: He ate two apples yesterday evening. He loves eating apples; he has already eaten one and wants to eat more.

words.pinyin: yǐjīng chī le yí ge le

subsections.title: Completed Action (Action + 了)
subsections.explanation: Put 了 right after the action word or phrase to show it is done, like “he went to class” or “I saw the doctor.”

patternRows.english: He has already arrived.

subsections.title: Counting Amounts: One 了 vs Two 了's
subsections.explanation: One 了 means the action finished in the past (“I drank two cups yesterday”). Two 了's mean you reached that number so far and might do more (“I have already drunk two cups, and want another”).

patternRows.english: I drank two cups of coffee yesterday (Single 了: completed in past).
I have already drunk two cups of coffee so far (Double 了: may continue).

grammarPages.learnerPromise: Distinguish between actions that did not happen in the past (沒) and actions that have not happened yet (還沒).
grammarPages.explanation: To say someone did not do an action in the past, use 沒 instead of 不. When an action hasn’t happened yet but you expect to do it later, use 還沒.

items.question: He did not come yesterday — 沒 or 還沒?
items.answer: 沒. Yesterday is finished, so the chance to come is over. 還沒 is for something still waiting to happen.

right.english: He did not come yesterday.

items.question: “I have not decided yet” — 還沒 or 還不?
items.answer: 還沒. 還不 sounds like you refuse. 還沒 says the decision has not happened up to now.

right.english: I have not decided yet.

items.question: After 沒, do I keep the 了?
items.answer: No. 沒 already says it did not happen, so there is no finished action to mark. Drop 了.

right.english: I did not do the homework.

discoveryLab.title: Move the timeline to NOW
discoveryLab.description: 沒 says the event did not happen. 還沒 says it is still not done at this moment.

subsections.title: Did Not Happen (沒 + Action)
subsections.explanation: Use 沒 before the action to say someone didn’t do it. Never use 不 or 了 here: say “he didn’t come” or “Dad didn’t drink coffee.” To ask if someone did it, add 了沒 at the end.

subsections.title: Not Yet (還沒 + Action)

items.question: “How did you meet?” — do I answer with 了?
items.answer: No. The question asks how, so 是…的 puts the spotlight on the way you met. 了 alone would only say it happened.

right.english: We met online.

items.question: Where does the detail go in a 是…的 sentence?
items.answer: Between 是 and the action word. The way you met comes before 認識.

right.english: I met him online.

items.question: Do I need the 的 at the end?
items.answer: Yes. 是…的 works as a pair. Without the ending 的, the sentence loses its spotlight.

right.english: He returned home yesterday.

discoveryLab.title: Move the spotlight

grammarPages.pattern: 先 + first action，等 + condition，再 + later action

items.question: Which step does 先 start?
items.answer: 先 starts the first action. 等 names what you wait for, and 再 starts the later action.

items.question: Is it 在 or 再 for the later step?
items.answer: 再. It means “then; after that”. 在 talks about where something is.

right.english: Decide first, then arrange a time.

items.question: Can 再 start the first step?
items.answer: No. 再 belongs to the later action. 先 opens the plan.

grammarPages.pattern: Person + 給 + receiver + action

patternRows.english: I write a card to my friend.
My older brother calls me.

items.question: “Write a card to a friend” — 給 or 跟?
items.answer: 給. The friend gets the card. 跟 goes with someone — like meeting or chatting together.

right.english: I write a card to my friend.

items.question: Where does the person who gets it go?
items.answer: Right after 給, before the action. 給 + person + action.

right.english: I write a card to my friend.

items.question: How do I say “my brother did not call me”?
items.answer: Put 給我 before 打電話. The person who gets the call comes right after 給.

text.traditional: 妳跟那位新朋友見面了沒有？
text.simplified: 你跟那位新朋友见面了没有？
text.pinyin: Nǐ gēn nà wèi xīn péngyǒu jiànmiàn le méiyǒu?
text.english: Have you met up with your new friend yet?

text.traditional: 我還沒決定要不要跟他見面。
text.simplified: 我还没决定要不要跟他见面。
text.pinyin: Wǒ hái méi juédìng yào bú yào gēn tā jiànmiàn.
text.english: I haven’t decided to meet him or not.

text.traditional: 妳擔心什麼？
text.simplified: 你担心什么？
text.pinyin: Nǐ dānxīn shénme?
text.english: What are you worried about?

text.traditional: 我有點兒緊張，我以前沒有這種經驗，所以覺得這樣有點兒奇怪。
text.simplified: 我有点儿紧张，我以前没有这种经验，所以觉得这样有点儿奇怪。
text.pinyin: Wǒ yǒudiǎnr jǐnzhāng, wǒ yǐqián méiyǒu zhè zhǒng jīngyàn, suǒyǐ juéde zhèyàng yǒudiǎnr qíguài.
text.english: I am a little nervous. I have never had an experience like this before, so I think it is a little strange.

text.traditional: 妳不要緊張，我有辦法，我跟妳一起去。
text.simplified: 你不要紧张，我有办法，我跟你一起去。
text.pinyin: Nǐ bú yào jǐnzhāng, wǒ yǒu bànfǎ, wǒ gēn nǐ yìqǐ qù.
text.english: Don’t be nervous. I have an idea: I can be there for you.

text.traditional: 太好了，謝謝妳幫我的忙。
text.simplified: 太好了，谢谢你帮我的忙。
text.pinyin: Tài hǎo le, xièxie nǐ bāng wǒ de máng.
text.english: Great! Thank you for helping me.

text.traditional: 不客氣。妳打算什麼時候跟他見面？
text.simplified: 不客气。你打算什么时候跟他见面？
text.pinyin: Bú kèqi. Nǐ dǎsuàn shénme shíhou gēn tā jiànmiàn?
text.english: You’re welcome. When do you plan to meet him?

text.traditional: 可能這個週末吧。如果妳有空，我再跟他約時間。
text.simplified: 可能这个周末吧。如果你有空，我再跟他约时间。
text.pinyin: Kěnéng zhège zhōumò ba. Rúguǒ nǐ yǒukòng, wǒ zài gēn tā yuē shíjiān.
text.english: Maybe this weekend. If you are free, I will arrange a time with him.

text.traditional: 有空啊，但是我明天不會來學校，等妳決定了，再給我打電話吧。
text.simplified: 有空啊，但是我明天不会来学校，等你决定了，再给我打电话吧。
