items.question: I write letters using Chinese. Where does 中文 go?
items.answer: 中文 is the tool, so it goes right after 用, before the action: 用中文寫信.

right.english: I write letters using Chinese.

items.question: Can you write with a brush — do I still need 用?
items.answer: Yes. 用 stays between 會 and the tool: 會用毛筆寫字. English drops the word “use”; Chinese does not.

items.question: I chat with friends in Chinese — 用 or 跟 before 中文?
items.answer: 用. 用 names the language or tool. 跟 is for the person you do it with: 跟朋友.

right.pinyin: Wǒ yòng Zhōngwén gēn péngyǒu liáotiān.
right.english: I chat with friends in Chinese.

grammarPages.titleEnglish: Place 以前 and 以後 on the Timeline
grammarPages.learnerPromise: Use 以前 and 以後 as standalone time words, after specific times, and after action statements.
grammarPages.explanation: 以前 means “before” or “in the past”; 以後 means “after” or “in the future.” You can use them on their own, or put them right after a time or an activity.

lessonWorld.title: Meet Zhongming’s past and future
lessonWorld.prompt: Zhongming’s old plan and future plan are different.
lessonWorld.traditional: 我以前想當老闆，現在想當醫生。
lessonWorld.simplified: 我以前想当老板，现在想当医生。
lessonWorld.pinyin: Wǒ yǐqián xiǎng dāng lǎobǎn, xiànzài xiǎng dāng yīshēng.
lessonWorld.english: I previously wanted to be a boss; now I want to be a doctor.

teachingGlossary.meaning: done; shows a change or finished action
links an action to how it went

grammarPages.pattern: 獨立時間詞 ｜ 時間點＋以前／以後 ｜ 句子＋以前／以後

patternRows.english: He was previously a teacher.

complement.meaning: I must arrive at the bank

complement.pinyin: wǒ rènshi le hěnduō xīn péngyǒu

patternRows.english: After coming to Taiwan, I made many new friends.

items.question: I go home before three. Where does 以前 go?
items.answer: Right after the time: 三點以前. 我以前三點回家 means something else — “I used to go home at three.”

right.pinyin: Wǒ sān diǎn yǐqián huí jiā.
right.english: I go home before three.

items.question: I want to be a reporter after graduating. Where does 以後 go?
items.answer: Right after the event: 畢業以後. Put it before the event and 以後畢業 means “graduate later.”

right.english: After graduating, I will become a reporter.

items.question: I want to be a reporter someday. Is 半年以後 okay?
items.answer: No. 半年以後 means “six months from now.” For a someday plan, use plain 以後.

right.english: I will become a reporter someday.

discoveryLab.title: Move 以前 and change the meaning
discoveryLab.description: Both sentences are correct. Position tells the listener what 以前 belongs to.

choices.label: Used to
choices.pinyin: Wǒ yǐqián sān diǎn huí jiā.
choices.english: I used to go home at three.
choices.note: 以前 points broadly to a previous period of life.

choices.label: Before 3:00
choices.pinyin: Wǒ sān diǎn yǐqián huí jiā.
choices.english: I go home before three.
choices.note: 三點 anchors the exact boundary.

choices.label: After work
choices.english: I am free after work.
choices.note: 下班 is the event boundary.

choices.label: Future career
choices.english: I want to be a reporter in the future.
choices.note: 以後 points broadly forward from now.

discoveryLab.takeaway: Before or after what? Place that time or event directly before 以前／以後.

subsections.title: Before or After a Time (Time + 以前 / 以後)

grammarPages.learnerPromise: Use 對 to indicate who you speak to, what something affects, and how someone is treated.
grammarPages.explanation: 對 points toward someone or something. Use it to speak toward someone, to say something is good or bad for your health, or to describe how someone treats others.

lessonWorld.title: Meet Guoan’s coworkers
lessonWorld.prompt: Guoan enjoys the bakery because his coworkers treat him well.
lessonWorld.traditional: 同事都對我很好。

links an action to how it went

grammarPages.pattern: 對人說話 ｜ 影響與益處 ｜ 對待態度

patternRows.english: I am telling this only to you; do not tell anyone else.
Using a phone often is bad for the eyes.
The boss treats us very well.

items.question: The boss is kind to me. Why does 我 come so early?
items.answer: 對 points at the receiver, so 我 follows it right away: 對我好. English puts “to me” at the end; Chinese does not.

right.english: The boss is kind to me.

items.question: My coworkers are kind to me. Did I say it right with 我對同事很好?
items.answer: No — you turned the arrow around. The person right after 對 receives the kindness, so it is 同事對我很好.

right.english: My coworkers are kind to me.

items.question: Phones are bad for my eyes — 對 or 跟 before 眼睛?
items.answer: 對. 對 shows where the effect lands. 跟 is for doing something together with someone.

right.english: Phones are bad for the eyes.

discoveryLab.title: Reverse the arrow, reverse the meaning
discoveryLab.description: Both directions can be grammatical. The arrow tells you who affects whom.

choices.label: Boss → me
choices.english: The boss is kind to me.

choices.label: Me → boss
choices.english: I am kind to the boss.
choices.note: The boss receives my kindness.

choices.label: Phone → eyes
choices.pinyin: Cháng yòng shǒujī duì yǎnjing bù hǎo.
choices.english: Frequent phone use is bad for the eyes.
choices.note: 眼睛 receives the negative effect.

discoveryLab.takeaway: Read the arrow: source → 對 → receiver → attitude or effect.

text.traditional: 他常對我說：「我們應該要多運動、多喝水。」
text.simplified: 他常对我说：「我们应该要多运动、多喝水。」
text.pinyin: Tā cháng duì wǒ shuō: "Wǒmen yīnggāi yào duō yùndòng, duō hē shuǐ."
text.english: He often says to me: "We should exercise more and drink more water."

text.traditional: 這件事我只對你說，你不要告訴別人。
text.simplified: 这件事我只对你说，你不要告诉别人。
text.pinyin: Zhè jiàn shì wǒ zhǐ duì nǐ shuō, nǐ bú yào gàosù biérén.
text.english: I am telling this only to you; please do not tell anyone else.

text.traditional: 常用手機對眼睛不好。
text.simplified: 常用手机对眼睛不好。
text.pinyin: Cháng yòng shǒujī duì yǎnjīng bù hǎo.
text.english: Using a mobile phone often is bad for your eyes.

text.traditional: 這本書對我不難，我可以學學看。
text.simplified: 这本书对我不难，我可以学学看。
text.pinyin: Zhè běn shū duì wǒ bù nán, wǒ kěyǐ xuéxue kàn.
text.english: This book is not difficult for me; I can try to learn it.

text.traditional: 他對我很好，常常幫我的忙。
text.simplified: 他对很好，常常帮我的忙。
text.pinyin: Tā duì wǒ hěn hǎo, chángcháng bāng wǒ de máng.
text.english: He treats me very well and often helps me.

text.traditional: A: 老闆對你們怎麼樣？ B: 他對我們很不錯，常常要我們多注意身體健康。
text.simplified: A: 老板对你们怎么样？ B: 他对我们很不错，常常要我们多注意身体健康。
text.pinyin: A: Lǎobǎn duì nǐmen zěnmeyàng? B: Tā duì wǒmen hěn búcuò, chángcháng yào wǒmen duō zhùyì shēntǐ jiànkāng.
text.english: A: How does the boss treat you? B: He treats us very well, often telling us to pay attention to our health.

questions.repairFeedback: Use 對你說.

questions.repairFeedback: Use 對我不難.

questions.repairFeedback: Use 對我很好.

subsections.title: Speaking to Someone (對 + Person + 說)
subsections.explanation: Put 對 before the person you are speaking to, like “he often says to me” (他常對我說).

patternRows.english: He often says to me: should exercise more.

subsections.title: Good or Bad for Something (對 + Body / Thing + 好 / 不好)
subsections.explanation: Say what is affected after 對, like “looking at phones often is bad for your eyes” (對眼睛不好).

patternRows.english: Using a phone often is bad for the eyes.

subsections.title: Treating Someone Well or Kindly (對 + Person + 很好)
subsections.explanation: Describe how someone treats people around them, like “the boss is very nice to us” (老闆對我們很不錯).

patternRows.english: The boss treats us very well.

dialogue.title: 對話一 · Dialogue 1
dialogue.setting: 在學校 · At school

text.traditional: 你昨天怎麼沒來上課？
text.simplified: 你昨天怎么没来上课？
text.pinyin: Nǐ zuótiān zěnme méi lái shàngkè?
text.english: How come you didn’t come to class yesterday?

text.traditional: 我去參加畫畫比賽。你們上課上了什麼？
text.simplified: 我去参加画画比赛。你们上课上了什么？
text.pinyin: Wǒ qù cānjiā huàhuà bǐsài. Nǐmen shàngkè shàng le shénme?
text.english: I participated in a drawing competition. What was the class about?

words.meaning: done; shows a change or finished action

text.traditional: 老師問我們想做什麼工作，大家都說得很高興。
text.simplified: 老师问我们想做什么工作，大家都说得很高兴。
text.pinyin: Lǎoshī wèn wǒmen xiǎng zuò shénme gōngzuò, dàjiā dōu shuō de hěn gāoxìng.
text.english: The teacher asked us what jobs we want to do. Everybody enjoyed talking about it.

words.meaning: links an action to how it went

text.traditional: 我知道友美想當護理師。別的同學呢？
text.simplified: 我知道友美想当护理师。别的同学呢？
text.pinyin: Wǒ zhīdào Yǒuměi xiǎng dāng hùlǐshī. Bié de tóngxué ne?
text.english: I know that Youmei wants to be a nurse. How about the others?

text.traditional: 宜文希望可以用中文和英文工作，所以她以後想當記者，元真想在銀行工作。
text.simplified: 宜文希望可以用中文和英文工作，所以她以后想当记者，元真想在银行工作。
text.pinyin: Yíwén xīwàng kěyǐ yòng Zhōngwén hé Yīngwén gōngzuò, suǒyǐ tā yǐhòu xiǎng dāng jìzhě, Yuánzhēn xiǎng zài yínháng gōngzuò.
text.english: Yiwen wants a job which requires Chinese and English language skills, so she wants to be a reporter in the future. Yuanzhen wants to work for a bank.

text.traditional: 那你畢業以後想做什麼？
text.simplified: 那你毕业以后想做什么？
text.pinyin: Nà nǐ bìyè yǐhòu xiǎng zuò shénme?
text.english: What job do you want to do after you graduate from school?

text.traditional: 我以前想當大公司的老闆，可是老闆要做的事情太多，現在覺得當醫生比較好。那你想做什麼？
text.simplified: 我以前想当大公司的老板，可是老板要做的事情太多，现在觉得当医生比较好。那你想做什么？
text.pinyin: Wǒ yǐqián xiǎng dāng dà gōngsī de lǎobǎn, kěshì lǎobǎn yào zuò de shìqing tài duō, xiànzài juéde dāng yīshēng bǐjiào hǎo. Nà nǐ xiǎng zuò shénme?
text.english: I wanted to be a business owner, but there are so many things to do as a business owner. Now I think being a doctor is better. What do you want to do then?

text.traditional: 當醫生很不錯，但是太忙了，我只想每天可以準時上班、下班。
text.simplified: 当医生很不错，但是太忙了，我只想每天可以准时上班、下班。
text.pinyin: Dāng yīshēng hěn búcuò, dànshì tài máng le, wǒ zhǐ xiǎng měitiān kěyǐ zhǔnshí shàngbān、xiàbān.
text.english: Being a doctor is great, but doctors are too busy. I just want to clock in and clock out on time.

comprehension.hint: Listen for her future plan after 以後.

items.title: Grammar 4–5 · Experience and life moments

grammarPages.lessonTitleEnglish: What Job Do You Want to Do?
grammarPages.titleTraditional: 在經驗履歷上蓋一個過
grammarPages.titleEnglish: Mark a Life Experience with 過
grammarPages.learnerPromise: Talk about past experiences with 過 and state completed actions with 過了.
grammarPages.explanation: Use 過 after an action word to talk about life experience—something you have ever done before. When paired with 了 at the end, it means you already did it today, so you don’t need to do it again.

lessonWorld.title: Open Zhongming’s work history
lessonWorld.prompt: Zhongming has worked in a restaurant before.
lessonWorld.traditional: 我以前在餐廳上過班。
lessonWorld.simplified: 我以前在餐厅上过班。
lessonWorld.pinyin: Wǒ yǐqián zài cāntīng shàngguo bān.
lessonWorld.english: I have worked in a restaurant before.

teachingGlossary.meaning: done; shows a change or finished action
links an action to how it went

grammarPages.pattern: 經驗：V + 過 ｜ 完成：V + 過 + 了

patternRows.english: I have seen this movie before.
Many Taiwanese people have been to Japan.
I have already eaten breakfast.
She has already been here.

items.question: Have you ever tried stinky tofu — 吃了 or 吃過?
items.answer: 吃過. 了 asks about one finished meal. 過 asks whether it ever happened in your life.

right.english: Have you ever tried stinky tofu?

items.question: I have worked at a restaurant. Where does 過 go?
items.answer: Between the two parts of 上班: 上過班. It cannot sit at the end of the whole action.

right.english: I have worked at a restaurant before.

items.question: I have not been to Japan — 不 or 沒 before 去過?
items.answer: 沒. 沒 says the experience never happened. 不 says you refuse or will not do it.

right.english: I have not been to Japan.

discoveryLab.title: Event or life experience?
discoveryLab.description: Both forms can be correct. Choose the viewpoint the question needs.

choices.label: Last year
choices.english: I went to Japan last year.
choices.note: 了 reports a particular trip in a dated story.

choices.label: Ever before
choices.english: I have been to Japan before.
choices.note: 過 adds Japan to the speaker’s life experience.

choices.label: Tried it?
choices.english: Have you ever tried stinky tofu?
choices.note: No exact date is needed; the question asks about experience.

discoveryLab.takeaway: Particular event? Use the event form. Ever in your experience? Use 過.

text.traditional: 很多台灣人去過日本，因為從台灣到日本不遠。
text.simplified: 很多台湾人去过日本，因为从台湾到日本不远。
text.pinyin: Hěnduō Táiwānrén qùguo Rìběn, yīnwèi cóng Táiwān dào Rìběn bù yuǎn.
text.english: Many Taiwanese have been to Japan, because it is not far from Taiwan to Japan.

text.traditional: A: 他來過我們家嗎？ B: 來過，那個時候你不在家。
text.simplified: A: 他来过我们家吗？ B: 来过，那个时候你不在家。
text.pinyin: A: Tā láiguo wǒmen jiā ma? B: Láiguo, nàge shíhou nǐ bù zài jiā.
text.english: A: Has he ever been to our home? B: Yes, he came; you weren't home at that time.

text.traditional: A: 你吃過臭豆腐嗎？ B: 我還沒吃過，聽說很特別。
text.simplified: A: 你吃过臭豆腐吗？ B: 我还没吃过，听说很特别。
text.pinyin: A: Nǐ chīguo chòudòufu ma? B: Wǒ hái méi chīguo, tīngshuō hěn tèbié.
text.english: A: Have you eaten stinky tofu? B: I haven't tried it yet; I hear it is unique.

text.traditional: A: 你要跟我們一起吃午飯嗎？ B: 我吃過了，你們去吃吧！
text.simplified: A: 你要跟我们一起吃午饭吗？ B: 我吃过了，你们去吃吧！
text.pinyin: A: Nǐ yào gēn wǒmen yìqǐ chī wǔfàn ma? B: Wǒ chīguo le, nǐmen qù chī ba!
text.english: A: Do you want to eat lunch with us? B: I've already eaten; you all go ahead!

text.traditional: A: 李小姐今天要來我們公司，她來過了嗎？ B: 她來過了，是早上來的。
text.simplified: A: 李小姐今天要来我们公司，她来过了吗？ B: 她来过了，是早上来的。
text.pinyin: A: Lǐ xiǎojiě jīntiān yào lái wǒmen gōngsī, tā láiguo le ma? B: Tā láiguo le, shì zǎoshang lái de.
text.english: A: Miss Li is visiting our company today; has she already come? B: She has already been here; she came in the morning.

text.traditional: A: 他給大家寫了一張卡片，你們都看過了嗎？ B: 我看過了。 C: 我還沒看。
text.simplified: A: 他给大家写了一张卡片，你们都看过了吗？ B: 我看过了。 C: 我还没看。
text.pinyin: A: Tā gěi dàjiā xiě le yì zhāng kǎpiàn, nǐmen dōu kànguo le ma? B: Wǒ kànguo le. C: Wǒ hái méi kàn.
text.english: A: He wrote a card for everyone, have you all read it yet? B: I have already read it. C: I haven't read it yet.

grammarPages.exerciseInstruction: Complete each experience sentence.

questions.repairFeedback: Use 吃過臭豆腐.

questions.repairFeedback: Use 上過班.

segments.hint: Use V + 過了 to indicate you already ate.

questions.correctFeedback: 吃過了 indicates the meal was completed and does not need repeating.
questions.repairFeedback: Use 吃過了.

segments.traditional: 李小姐今天要來我們公司，她

segments.hint: Ask whether she has already visited.

questions.correctFeedback: 來過了嗎 asks if the scheduled visit already occurred.

questions.correctFeedback: 看過了嗎 checks completion before the present moment.
questions.repairFeedback: Use 看過了嗎.

subsections.title: Life Experience (Ever Done with 過)
subsections.explanation: Put 過 right after the action word to share something you have experienced at least once in your life, like “I have been to Japan.” Say 沒...過 for things you have never done.

patternRows.english: I have seen this movie.
Many Taiwanese people have been to Japan.

subsections.title: Already Done for Now (過 ... 了)
subsections.explanation: Use 過 with 了 at the end when an action was already completed earlier today and doesn’t need to be repeated, like “I already ate breakfast” or “I’ve already read the note.”

patternRows.english: I have eaten breakfast.
She has already been here.

grammarPages.lessonTitleEnglish: What Job Do You Want to Do?
grammarPages.titleEnglish: Open a Moment with …的時候
grammarPages.learnerPromise: Say what happens during a situation or moment.
grammarPages.explanation: Put the event or situation before 的時候. Then say what happens inside that moment.

lessonWorld.title: Open a moment at the bakery
lessonWorld.prompt: Guoan will ask the boss when he sees him tomorrow.
lessonWorld.traditional: 我看到老闆的時候，幫你問他。
lessonWorld.simplified: 我看到老板的时候，帮你问他。
lessonWorld.pinyin: Wǒ kàndào lǎobǎn de shíhou, bāng nǐ wèn tā.
lessonWorld.english: When I see the boss, I will ask him for you.

teachingGlossary.meaning: done; shows a change or finished action
links an action to how it went

grammarPages.pattern: Situation + 的時候，what happens

patternRows.english: Chat while eating.
Listen to music when unhappy.
Drink water while exercising.

items.question: When working, I use Chinese — is it 工作時候 or 工作的時候?
items.answer: Keep 的. 的 connects the situation to 時候: 工作的時候.

right.english: When working, speak Chinese.

items.question: When I feel unhappy, I listen to music. Where does 不好 go?
items.answer: Keep the situation together: 心情不好, then 的時候. 的時候 needs the whole situation before it.

right.traditional: 心情不好的時候，聽音樂。
right.simplified: 心情不好的时候，听音乐。
right.pinyin: Xīnqíng bù hǎo de shíhou, tīng yīnyuè.
right.english: When I feel unhappy, I listen to music.

items.question: I drink water while exercising. Is 運動以後 okay?
items.answer: No. 運動以後 means after exercising. For inside the moment, use 運動的時候.

right.pinyin: Yùndòng de shíhou, wǒ hē shuǐ.
right.english: When exercising, I drink water.

liveSceneLab.title: Open a different life moment
liveSceneLab.description: The moment changes; 的時候 keeps the situation attached to what happens inside it.

choices.label: Eating
choices.subject: 我
choices.traditional: 吃飯的時候，我不用手機。
choices.simplified: 吃饭的时候，我不用手机。
choices.pinyin: Chīfàn de shíhou, wǒ bú yòng shǒujī.
choices.english: When eating, I do not use my phone.
choices.note: 吃飯 names the moment.

choices.label: Feeling down
choices.subject: 我
choices.traditional: 心情不好的時候，我會聽音樂。
choices.simplified: 心情不好的时候，我会听音乐。
choices.pinyin: Xīnqíng bù hǎo de shíhou, wǒ huì tīng yīnyuè.
choices.english: When I feel unhappy, I listen to music.
choices.note: A state can open the moment window.

choices.label: At work
choices.subject: 我
choices.traditional: 工作的時候，我常常說中文。
choices.simplified: 工作的时候，我常常说中文。
choices.pinyin: Gōngzuò de shíhou, wǒ chángcháng shuō Zhōngwén.
choices.english: When working, I often speak Chinese.
choices.note: 工作 is the situation.

liveSceneLab.takeaway: Name the moment first: situation + 的時候. Then say what happens.

examples.teachingNote: A weather situation opens the moment.

text.traditional: 天氣好的時候，我喜歡出去運動。
text.simplified: 天气好的时候，我喜欢出去运动。
text.pinyin: Tiānqì hǎo de shíhou, wǒ xǐhuān chūqù yùndòng.
text.english: When the weather is good, I like exercising outside.

examples.teachingNote: A routine rule inside a moment.

text.traditional: 在我們家，吃飯的時候，不可以用手機。
text.simplified: 在我们家，吃饭的时候，不可以用手机。
text.pinyin: Zài wǒmen jiā, chīfàn de shíhou, bù kěyǐ yòng shǒujī.
text.english: In our home, do not use a phone while eating.

examples.teachingNote: A complete action can name the moment.

text.traditional: 他玩電腦的時候，都不跟別人說話。
text.simplified: 他玩电脑的时候，都不跟别人说话。
text.pinyin: Tā wán diànnǎo de shíhou, dōu bù gēn biérén shuōhuà.
text.english: When he uses the computer, he does not talk to others.

examples.teachingNote: A feeling can name the moment.

text.traditional: 我心情不好的時候，都會聽音樂、跟朋友聊天。
text.simplified: 我心情不好的时候，都会听音乐、跟朋友聊天。
text.pinyin: Wǒ xīnqíng bù hǎo de shíhou, dōu huì tīng yīnyuè, gēn péngyǒu liáotiān.
text.english: When I feel unhappy, I listen to music and chat with friends.

dialogue.title: 對話二 · Dialogue 2
dialogue.setting: 談打工經驗 · Discussing work experience

text.traditional: 國安，你每天下課以後都要去麵包店工作，辛苦嗎？
text.simplified: 国安，你每天下课以后都要去面包店工作，辛苦吗？
text.pinyin: Guó’ān, nǐ měitiān xiàkè yǐhòu dōu yào qù miànbāodiàn gōngzuò, xīnkǔ ma?
text.english: Guoan, you work at the bakery everyday after school. Is it tiring?

text.traditional: 不辛苦。我很喜歡這個工作，因為可以學怎麼做麵包，而且同事也都對我很好。
text.simplified: 不辛苦。我很喜欢这个工作，因为可以学怎么做面包，而且同事也都对我很好。
text.pinyin: Bù xīnkǔ. Wǒ hěn xǐhuān zhège gōngzuò, yīnwèi kěyǐ xué zěnme zuò miànbāo, érqiě tóngshì yě dōu duì wǒ hěn hǎo.
text.english: It’s okay. I like this job very much because I get to learn how to make bread. Moreover, the colleagues are very nice to me as well.

text.traditional: 這樣你在學校的成績，不會有問題嗎？
text.simplified: 这样你在学校的成绩，不会有问题吗？
text.pinyin: Zhèyàng nǐ zài xuéxiào de chéngjì, bú huì yǒu wèntí ma?
text.english: Does it affect your studies?

text.traditional: 不會啊！我都先做功課，再去工作。
text.simplified: 不会啊！我都先做功课，再去工作。
text.pinyin: Bú huì a! Wǒ dōu xiān zuò gōngkè, zài qù gōngzuò.
text.english: No, it doesn’t. I always do my homework first, and then go to work.

text.traditional: 我以前在餐廳上過班，因為太累了，常常睡得不夠。
text.simplified: 我以前在餐厅上过班，因为太累了，常常睡得不够。
text.pinyin: Wǒ yǐqián zài cāntīng shàngguo bān, yīnwèi tài lèi le, chángcháng shuì de bú gòu.
text.english: I have worked at a restaurant before. I was exhausted, and always didn’t get enough sleep.

links an action to how it went

text.traditional: 這樣真的很辛苦。
text.simplified: 这样真的很辛苦。
text.pinyin: Zhèyàng zhēn de hěn xīnkǔ.
text.english: It is really tiring.

text.traditional: 有時候早上起得太晚，上課遲到了，而且沒時間準備考試，所以就不做了。
text.simplified: 有时候早上起得太晚，上课迟到了，而且没时间准备考试，所以就不做了。
text.pinyin: Yǒushíhou zǎoshang qǐ de tài wǎn, shàngkè chídào le, érqiě méi shíjiān zhǔnbèi kǎoshì, suǒyǐ jiù bú zuò le.
text.english: Sometimes I got up late, so I was late for school. Moreover, I didn’t have the time to prepare for the exams. So I quit.

text.traditional: 我下午四點到六點上班，工作時間不長，所以沒問題。
text.simplified: 我下午四点到六点上班，工作时间不长，所以没问题。
text.pinyin: Wǒ xiàwǔ sì diǎn dào liù diǎn shàngbān, gōngzuò shíjiān bù cháng, suǒyǐ méi wèntí.
text.english: I work from 4 to 6 p.m. Working hours are not long, so I am all right.

text.traditional: 兩個小時也可以嗎？那你們麵包店還需要人嗎？
text.simplified: 两个小时也可以吗？那你们面包店还需要人吗？

text.english: Is it okay to work two hours? Does your bakery still need employees?

text.traditional: 不知道。我明天看到老闆的時候，幫你問他。
text.simplified: 不知道。我明天看到老板的时候，帮你问他。
text.pinyin: Bù zhīdào. Wǒ míngtiān kàndào lǎobǎn de shíhou, bāng nǐ wèn tā.

items.title: Grammar 1–3 · Quick actions, directions, and route results

grammarPages.lessonTitleEnglish: Get on the Internet with a Cell Phone
grammarPages.titleTraditional: 讓動作變得輕鬆、短一點
grammarPages.titleEnglish: Make an Action Light with V(一)V
grammarPages.learnerPromise: Suggest a short, casual action.
grammarPages.explanation: Repeat a short action word, with or without 一, to make the action feel brief, casual, or low-pressure.

lessonWorld.title: Get to the museum before it opens
lessonWorld.prompt: Guoan sends the museum website. Zhongming takes a quick look.
lessonWorld.traditional: 你可以先看看。
lessonWorld.simplified: 你可以先看看。
lessonWorld.pinyin: Nǐ kěyǐ xiān kànkan.
lessonWorld.english: You can take a quick look first.

grammarPages.pattern: Action verb + action verb / Action verb + 一 + action verb

patternRows.english: I take a quick look at my phone.
I listen to some music.
We chat for a bit.

items.question: Does 看看 mean I look two times?
items.answer: No. Doubling the action word makes it short and casual — “for a bit.” 兩次 counts an exact number.

right.english: I want to take a look.

items.question: 聊天 already has two parts. Can I double the whole word?
items.answer: No. Double only the first part: 聊聊天. The rest of the word stays the same.

right.english: Let us chat for a bit.

items.question: I already took a look. Is it 看看了?
items.answer: No. For a finished quick look, put 了 between the two parts: 看了看.

right.english: I took a quick look at my phone.

discoveryLab.title: Short action, not two actions
discoveryLab.description: Repeating the action word softens it. It does not count exactly twice.

choices.label: Quick look
choices.english: I want to take a look.
choices.note: 看看 makes the request feel light.

choices.label: Exactly twice
choices.english: I want to look twice.
choices.note: 兩次 counts an exact number. 看看 does not.

choices.label: Listen a bit
choices.english: I want to listen to some music.
choices.note: The action feels relaxed and limited.

choices.label: Casual chat
choices.english: Let us chat for a bit.
choices.note: A two-part action like 聊天 can repeat its first part in this shape.

discoveryLab.takeaway: Do not translate the repeated verb as “twice.” Hear it as “for a bit.”

examples.teachingNote: Action verb reduplication softens the tone to indicate doing something casually.

text.traditional: 他週末常去打打球、看看電影。
text.simplified: 他周末常去打打球、看看电影。
text.pinyin: Tā zhōumò cháng qù dǎdǎ qiú, kànkan diànyǐng.
text.english: On weekends he often goes to play ball and watch movies.

examples.teachingNote: Two reduplicated verbs create a relaxed, casual picture of leisure time.

text.traditional: 我平常有空的時候，都在家上上網、玩玩手機。
text.simplified: 我平常有空的时候，都在家上上网、玩玩手机。
text.pinyin: Wǒ píngcháng yǒu kòng de shíhòu, dōu zài jiā shàngshàng wǎng, wánwán shǒujī.
text.english: When I have free time usually, I go online and play on my phone at home.

examples.teachingNote: A gentle social action.

text.traditional: 媽媽最近心情不太好，我們應該多跟她說說話。
text.simplified: 妈妈最近心情不太好，我们应该多跟她说说话。
text.pinyin: Māma zuìjìn xīnqíng bú tài hǎo, wǒmen yīnggāi duō gēn tā shuō shuōhuà.
text.english: Mom has been in a bad mood lately; we should talk with her more.

examples.teachingNote: Several casual actions can form a relaxed scene.

text.traditional: 上班的休息時間，我常跟同事一起喝喝咖啡、聊聊天。
text.simplified: 上班的休息时间，我常跟同事一起喝喝咖啡、聊聊天。
text.pinyin: Shàngbān de xiūxi shíjiān, wǒ cháng gēn tóngshì yìqǐ hēhe kāfēi, liáo liáotiān.
text.english: During breaks at work, I often have coffee and chat with coworkers.

grammarPages.exerciseInstruction: Complete each friendly suggestion.

questions.repairFeedback: Use the repeated verb for “take a look.”

grammarPages.lessonTitleEnglish: Get on the Internet with a Cell Phone
grammarPages.titleEnglish: Move from a Start toward a Direction
grammarPages.learnerPromise: Give a route using a clear start and direction.
grammarPages.explanation: 從 opens the starting point. 往 opens the direction or destination you move toward.

lessonWorld.title: Get to the museum before it opens
lessonWorld.prompt: The museum is near Guoan’s home.
lessonWorld.traditional: 從我家出去，往右轉。
lessonWorld.simplified: 从我家出去，往右转。
lessonWorld.pinyin: Cóng wǒ jiā chūqù, wǎng yòu zhuǎn.
lessonWorld.english: Go out from my home and turn right.

grammarPages.pattern: 從 + start + 往 + direction + action

patternRows.english: Walk from here toward the entrance.
Walk from my home toward the right.
Look forward from here.

items.question: I want to walk from my home toward the right. Which word is the start?
items.answer: 從 marks where you leave from; 往 marks the way you go. Put 從 first: 從我家往右邊走.

right.pinyin: Cóng wǒ jiā wǎng yòubiān zǒu.
right.english: Walk from my home toward the right.

items.question: Do I need a word before 我家 when I start moving?
items.answer: Yes — 從. It opens the starting point of the movement.

right.pinyin: Cóng wǒ jiā chūqù, wǎng yòu zhuǎn.
right.english: Go out from my home and turn right.

items.question: Can I use 到 instead of 往 for a direction?
items.answer: No. 到 means “arrive at a place.” 往 points the way you move, so use 往 for a direction.

right.english: Walk from here toward the entrance.

routeLab.title: Trace the route arrow
routeLab.description: Choose a route. The left point is 從; the arrow points 往 the destination.

choices.label: To the entrance
choices.english: Walk from here toward the entrance.
choices.note: 這裡 is the start; 門口 is the direction.

choices.label: Forward
choices.pinyin: Cóng wǒ jiā wǎng qián zǒu.
choices.english: Walk forward from my home.
choices.note: 往前 gives a direction rather than a named place.

choices.label: Look outside
choices.english: Look outside from the window.
choices.note: The eyes move from the window toward outside.

routeLab.takeaway: Find the start first. Then follow 往 toward the direction.

examples.teachingNote: A writing direction.

text.traditional: 中國字應該從左往右寫，韓國字呢？
text.simplified: 中国字应该从左往右写，韩国字呢？
text.pinyin: Zhōngguó zì yīnggāi cóng zuǒ wǎng yòu xiě, Hánguó zì ne?
text.english: Chinese characters should be written from left to right. What about Korean characters?

examples.teachingNote: A source-to-view direction.

text.traditional: 從我房間的窗戶往外看，就可以看到漂亮的風景。
text.simplified: 从我房间的窗户往外看，就可以看到漂亮的风景。
text.pinyin: Cóng wǒ fángjiān de chuānghu wǎng wài kàn, jiù kěyǐ kàndào piàoliang de fēngjǐng.
text.english: Looking outside from my room’s window, you can see beautiful scenery.

examples.teachingNote: A visible landmark gives the direction.

text.traditional: 從這裡往最高的那棟房子走，你會看到兩家百貨公司。
text.simplified: 从这里往最高的那栋房子走，你会看到两家百货公司。
text.pinyin: Cóng zhèlǐ wǎng zuì gāo de nà dòng fángzi zǒu, nǐ huì kàndào liǎng jiā bǎihuò gōngsī.
text.english: Walk from here toward the tallest building, and you will see two department stores.

grammarPages.exercisePreview: Place 從 at the start and 往 before the direction.
grammarPages.exerciseInstruction: Complete each route instruction.

segments.hint: Use 從 + start + 往 + direction.

tiles.meaning: walk from here toward the entrance

questions.correctFeedback: 這裡 is the start; 門口 is the direction.
questions.repairFeedback: Use 從 + start + 往 + direction.

segments.hint: Find start, then direction.

tiles.pinyin: cóng wǒ jiā wǎng yòu zǒu
wǒ jiā cóng yòu wǎng zǒu

questions.correctFeedback: 我家 follows 從; 右 follows 往.
questions.repairFeedback: Find start, then direction.

segments.hint: Use 從左往右.

questions.correctFeedback: Left is the start; right is the direction.
questions.repairFeedback: Use 從左往右.

grammarPages.lessonTitleEnglish: Get on the Internet with a Cell Phone
grammarPages.titleTraditional: 看懂就帶來的「早」和「結果」
grammarPages.titleEnglish: Read the Time and Result Meanings of 就
grammarPages.learnerPromise: Recognize something early or a result that follows.
grammarPages.explanation: In a time scene, 就 can mean earlier than expected. After an instruction or condition, 就 can introduce the result.

lessonWorld.title: Get to the museum before it opens
lessonWorld.prompt: The route is short: walk five minutes and you arrive.
lessonWorld.traditional: 往右走，五分鐘就到了。
lessonWorld.simplified: 往右走，五分钟就到了。
lessonWorld.pinyin: Wǎng yòu zǒu, wǔ fēnzhōng jiù dào le.
lessonWorld.english: Walk right and you will arrive in five minutes.

grammarPages.pattern: Time + 就 + action / Instruction， 就 + result

patternRows.english: Arrive as early as 8:30.
Walk ahead, then arrive.
Take a look first, then know.

items.question: He got to work at 8:30, before 9:00. 就 or 才?
items.answer: 就 — “as early as 8:30,” good news. 才 would say “not until 8:30,” which sounds too late.

right.pinyin: Tā bā diǎn bàn jiù dào le.
right.english: He arrived as early as 8:30.

items.question: Where does 就 sit in a result sentence?
items.answer: Right before the result action: 就 + action. Never after it.

right.english: Take a look first, then you will know.

items.question: I woke up at six. Do I need 了 at the end?
items.answer: Yes. An early finished moment uses the pair 就 + action + 了.

right.pinyin: Wǒ liù diǎn jiù qǐchuáng le.
right.english: I got up as early as six.

discoveryLab.title: Two scenes, two jobs for 就
discoveryLab.description: Do not force one English translation. Let the scene reveal the job.

choices.label: Earlier than expected
choices.traditional: 九點上班，我八點半就到了。
choices.simplified: 九点上班，我八点半就到了。
choices.pinyin: Jiǔ diǎn shàngbān, wǒ bā diǎn bàn jiù dào le.
choices.english: Work starts at nine; I arrived as early as 8:30.
choices.note: The expected time is nine. 就 highlights the early arrival.

choices.label: Then you see it
choices.traditional: 往前走，就可以看到博物館。
choices.simplified: 往前走，就可以看到博物馆。
choices.pinyin: Wǎng qián zǒu, jiù kěyǐ kàndào bówùguǎn.
choices.english: Walk forward, then you can see the museum.
choices.note: The first action produces the result after 就.

choices.label: Then it is fine
choices.traditional: 先跟老師請假，就沒問題了。
choices.simplified: 先跟老师请假，就没问题了。
choices.pinyin: Xiān gēn lǎoshī qǐngjià, jiù méi wèntí le.
choices.english: Ask the teacher for leave first; then there is no problem.
choices.note: 就 introduces the result of the solution.

discoveryLab.takeaway: Time scene: sooner than expected. Action scene: then this result follows.

examples.teachingNote: Earlier than expected.

text.traditional: 九點開始上班，可是我每天都八點半就到公司了。
text.simplified: 九点开始上班，可是我每天都八点半就到公司了。
text.pinyin: Jiǔ diǎn kāishǐ shàngbān, kěshì wǒ měitiān dōu bā diǎn bàn jiù dào gōngsī le.
text.english: Work starts at nine, but I arrive at the office by 8:30 every day.

examples.teachingNote: The time is surprisingly early.

text.traditional: 我今天早上六點就起床了。
text.simplified: 我今天早上六点就起床了。
text.pinyin: Wǒ jīntiān zǎoshang liù diǎn jiù qǐchuáng le.
text.english: I got up as early as six this morning.

examples.teachingNote: An instruction produces a result.

text.traditional: 你往前走，就可以看到那家店了。
text.simplified: 你往前走，就可以看到那家店了。
text.pinyin: Nǐ wǎng qián zǒu, jiù kěyǐ kàndào nà jiā diàn le.
text.english: Walk forward, then you can see the shop.

examples.teachingNote: A solution produces a result.

text.traditional: 你先跟老師請假，就沒問題了吧？
text.simplified: 你先跟老师请假，就没问题了吧？
text.pinyin: Nǐ xiān gēn lǎoshī qǐngjià, jiù méi wèntí le ba?
text.english: Ask the teacher for leave first; then there is no problem.

grammarPages.exercisePreview: Choose between an early-time signal and a following result.
grammarPages.exerciseInstruction: Complete the sentence that matches the scene.

segments.hint: The scene says 8:30 is early.

questions.correctFeedback: 就 highlights the earlier-than-expected arrival.
questions.repairFeedback: The scene says 8:30 is early.

segments.hint: Use 就 to open what follows.

questions.correctFeedback: The instruction produces the result.
questions.repairFeedback: Use 就 to open what follows.

segments.hint: Place 就 before the result action.

questions.correctFeedback: 就 introduces the result of checking.
questions.repairFeedback: Place 就 before the result action.

dialogue.title: 對話一 · Dialogue 1
dialogue.setting: 國安給中明打電話 · Guoan calls Zhongming

text.traditional: 喂，中明，半個小時以前我寄了一封電子郵件給你，你看到了嗎？
text.simplified: 喂，中明，半个小时以前我寄了一封电子邮件给你，你看到了吗？
text.pinyin: Wèi, Zhōngmíng, bàn ge xiǎoshí yǐqián wǒ jì le yì fēng diànzǐ yóujiàn gěi nǐ, nǐ kàndào le ma?
text.english: Hello, Zhongming, I sent you an email half an hour ago. Have you read it?

text.traditional: 剛剛我的手機網路有點兒問題，不能看電子郵件，你寄的是什麼？
text.simplified: 刚刚我的手机网路有点儿问题，不能看电子邮件，你寄的是什么？
text.pinyin: Gānggāng wǒ de shǒujī wǎnglù yǒudiǎnr wèntí, bù néng kàn diànzǐ yóujiàn, nǐ jì de shì shénme?
text.english: The internet connection on my phone just had a little problem; I couldn’t read your email. What did you send me?

text.traditional: 博物館的網址。下禮拜六老師要帶我們去參觀，你可以先看看。
text.simplified: 博物馆的网址。下礼拜六老师要带我们去参观，你可以先看看。
text.pinyin: Bówùguǎn de wǎngzhǐ. Xià lǐbàiliù lǎoshī yào dài wǒmen qù cānguān, nǐ kěyǐ xiān kànkan.
text.english: I sent you a link for the museum website. The teacher is taking us to visit there next Saturday; you can take a look first.

text.traditional: 好。（看看手機）現在沒問題了，我看到了。
text.simplified: 好。（看看手机）现在没问题了，我看到了。
text.pinyin: Hǎo. (Kànkan shǒujī) Xiànzài méi wèntí le, wǒ kàndào le.
text.english: OK. (Take a look at the phone) There’s no problem now, I’ve read your email.

text.traditional: 網站上有地址，那個地方在我家附近，從我家出去，往右轉，差不多五分鐘就到了。
text.simplified: 网站上有地址，那个地方在我家附近，从我家出去，往右转，差不多五分钟就到了。
text.pinyin: Wǎngzhàn shang yǒu dìzhǐ, nà ge dìfang zài wǒ jiā fùjìn, cóng wǒ jiā chūqù, wǎng yòu zhuǎn, chàbuduō wǔ fēnzhōng jiù dào le.
text.english: There’s the address on the website; that place is close to my house. If you go from my place, you make a right turn, and you’ll be there in just about five minutes.

text.traditional: 我們應該幾點到？
text.simplified: 我们应该几点到？
text.pinyin: Wǒmen yīnggāi jǐ diǎn dào?
text.english: What time should we be there?

text.traditional: 早上九點在博物館門口見，要記得準時到。
text.simplified: 早上九点在博物馆门口见，要记得准时到。
text.pinyin: Zǎoshang jiǔ diǎn zài bówùguǎn ménkǒu jiàn, yào jìde zhǔnshí dào.
text.english: 9 a.m. at the museum gate. Remember to get there on time.

text.traditional: 我們上個星期六去運動的時候，我到得太晚，真不好意思。下個星期我一定會準時。
text.simplified: 我们上个星期六去运动的时候，我到得太晚，真不好意思。下个星期我一定会准时。
text.pinyin: Wǒmen shàng ge xīngqīliù qù yùndòng de shíhou, wǒ dào de tài wǎn, zhēn bù hǎoyìsi. Xià ge xīngqī wǒ yídìng huì zhǔnshí.
text.english: I am sorry for being late when we went exercising last Saturday. I’ll definitely be on time next week.

comprehension.hint: Listen for the duration before 就到了.

items.title: Grammar 4–5 · Countdown and duration

grammarPages.lessonTitleEnglish: Get on the Internet with a Cell Phone
grammarPages.titleEnglish: Start a Countdown with 就要…了
grammarPages.learnerPromise: Say that an event is about to happen.
grammarPages.explanation: 就要 or 快要 places an event very near. Sentence-final 了 signals that the new situation is arriving.

lessonWorld.title: Get to the museum before it opens
lessonWorld.prompt: It is 8:55. The museum opens at nine.
lessonWorld.traditional: 博物館五分鐘以後就要開門了。
lessonWorld.simplified: 博物馆五分钟以后就要开门了。
lessonWorld.pinyin: Bówùguǎn wǔ fēnzhōng yǐhòu jiù yào kāimén le.
lessonWorld.english: The museum will open in five minutes.

grammarPages.pattern: Time clue + 就要／快要 + event + 了

patternRows.english: The doors will open in five minutes.
They are returning home tomorrow.
It is about to begin.

items.question: I want to say the doors are about to open. 就 or 就要?
items.answer: 就要. 要 carries the “about to” idea; 就 alone means “as early as” or “then.”

right.english: The museum is about to open.

items.question: He is about to go back home. Is 他回國就要了 right?
items.answer: No. Put 就要 before the event and 了 at the very end: 就要 + event + 了.

right.english: He is about to go back to his home country.

items.question: Zhongming is almost here. Where does 快要 go?
items.answer: Before the event: 快要 + event + 了. Never after it.

right.english: Zhongming is almost here.

discoveryLab.title: Match the countdown clock
discoveryLab.description: Choose the sentence whose event is close to the current moment.

choices.label: Doors open
choices.english: The museum is about to open.
choices.note: The closed doors and near opening time create the countdown.

choices.label: Movie starts
choices.pinyin: Diànyǐng mǎshàng jiù yào kāishǐ le.
choices.english: The movie is about to start.
choices.note: 馬上 strengthens the sense of “very soon.”

choices.label: Almost here
choices.english: Zhongming is almost here.
choices.note: 快要 works without 就 in this source pattern.

choices.label: Next month
choices.pinyin: Wǒ xià ge yuè jiù yào huíguó le.
choices.english: I will return home next month.
choices.note: A known approaching change can use the countdown frame.

discoveryLab.takeaway: Look for an approaching change: 就要／快要 + event + 了.

examples.teachingNote: An approaching future change.

text.traditional: 我下個月就要回國了。
text.simplified: 我下个月就要回国了。
text.pinyin: Wǒ xià ge yuè jiù yào huíguó le.
text.english: I will return home next month.

examples.teachingNote: A near arrival.

text.traditional: 他的女朋友明天就要來了，他非常開心。
text.simplified: 他的女朋友明天就要来了，他非常开心。
text.pinyin: Tā de nǚpéngyǒu míngtiān jiù yào lái le, tā fēicháng kāixīn.
text.english: His girlfriend is coming tomorrow; he is very happy.

examples.teachingNote: The source also allows 就 + event + 了 without 要.

text.traditional: 電影馬上就開始了，他怎麼還沒來？
text.simplified: 电影马上就开始了，他怎么还没来？
text.pinyin: Diànyǐng mǎshàng jiù kāishǐ le, tā zěnme hái méi lái?
text.english: The movie is about to start; why is he not here yet?

examples.teachingNote: A closing countdown.

text.traditional: 圖書館就要關了，你現在去也許太晚了。
text.simplified: 图书馆就要关了，你现在去也许太晚了。
text.pinyin: Túshūguǎn jiù yào guān le, nǐ xiànzài qù yěxǔ tài wǎn le.
text.english: The library is about to close; if you go now, it may be too late.

grammarPages.titleEnglish: Measure an Action’s Duration
grammarPages.learnerPromise: Say how long an action lasts.
grammarPages.explanation: Duration follows the action. With some activities that pair an action word with a thing, Chinese repeats the action word or uses duration + 的 before the thing.

lessonWorld.title: Measure the whole journey
lessonWorld.prompt: The group waits ten minutes and visits for three hours.
lessonWorld.traditional: 我們排隊排十分鐘，參觀三個小時。
lessonWorld.simplified: 我们排队排十分钟，参观三个小时。
lessonWorld.pinyin: Wǒmen páiduì pái shí fēnzhōng, cānguān sān ge xiǎoshí.
lessonWorld.english: We wait in line for ten minutes and visit for three hours.

grammarPages.pattern: Action + duration / Activity + action + duration

patternRows.english: Work for eight hours.
Run for thirty minutes.
Attend class for three hours.

items.question: I slept three hours. Can I say 我睡覺三個小時?
items.answer: No. A two-part action word needs its first part again: 睡了三個小時的覺 (or 睡覺睡三個小時).

right.pinyin: Wǒ shuì le sān ge xiǎoshí de jiào.
right.english: I slept for three hours.

items.question: Why does 睡 repeat AFTER 睡覺, not inside it?
items.answer: For duration, repeat the first action word after the whole word: 睡覺睡十分鐘. 睡睡覺 would mean “sleep a bit” — not a count of time.

right.english: I sleep for ten minutes.

items.question: I study Chinese for three hours. Where does the time go?
items.answer: With a thing after the action, use duration + 的 + thing: 學三個小時的中文.

right.pinyin: Wǒ xué sān ge xiǎoshí de Zhōngwén.
right.english: I study Chinese for three hours.

discoveryLab.title: Attach the clock to the action
discoveryLab.description: Start with the simplest shape, then watch what happens when the activity also names a thing.

choices.label: Work
choices.pinyin: Wǒ měitiān gōngzuò bā ge xiǎoshí.
choices.english: I work eight hours every day.
choices.note: A simple action can take duration directly.

choices.label: Sleep
choices.traditional: 我每天睡覺睡七個小時。
choices.simplified: 我每天睡觉睡七个小时。
choices.pinyin: Wǒ měitiān shuìjiào shuì qī ge xiǎoshí.
choices.english: I sleep seven hours every day.
choices.note: The action word from 睡覺 repeats before the duration.

choices.label: Class
choices.traditional: 我明天要上課上三個小時。
choices.simplified: 我明天要上课上三个小时。
choices.pinyin: Wǒ míngtiān yào shàngkè shàng sān ge xiǎoshí.
choices.english: I will attend class for three hours tomorrow.
choices.note: 上 repeats after the two-part activity 上課.

choices.label: Study Chinese
choices.traditional: 我每天學三個小時的中文。
choices.simplified: 我每天学三个小时的中文。
choices.pinyin: Wǒ měitiān xué sān ge xiǎoshí de Zhōngwén.
choices.english: I study Chinese for three hours every day.
choices.note: Duration + 的 can sit before the thing you study, 中文.

discoveryLab.takeaway: Keep the duration attached to the action—not floating at the end of the whole story.

examples.teachingNote: Simple action + duration.

text.traditional: 我每天工作八個小時。
text.simplified: 我每天工作八个小时。
text.pinyin: Wǒ měitiān gōngzuò bā ge xiǎoshí.
text.english: I work eight hours every day.

examples.teachingNote: Duration follows the action.

text.simplified: 爸爸每天早上运动三十分钟。
text.pinyin: Bàba měitiān zǎoshang yùndòng sānshí fēnzhōng.

text.traditional: 我每天跑步跑三十分鐘。
text.simplified: 我每天跑步跑三十分钟。
text.pinyin: Wǒ měitiān pǎobù pǎo sānshí fēnzhōng.
text.english: I run for thirty minutes every day.

examples.teachingNote: Duration + 的 appears before the thing.

text.traditional: 我明天要開六個小時的車。
text.simplified: 我明天要开六个小时的车。
text.pinyin: Wǒ míngtiān yào kāi liù ge xiǎoshí de chē.
text.english: I will drive for six hours tomorrow.

dialogue.title: 對話二 · Dialogue 2
dialogue.setting: 在博物館門口 · At the museum gate

text.traditional: 博物館五分鐘以後就要開門了，大家都到了吧？
text.simplified: 博物馆五分钟以后就要开门了，大家都到了吧？
text.pinyin: Bówùguǎn wǔ fēnzhōng yǐhòu jiù yào kāimén le, dàjiā dōu dào le ba?
text.english: The museum will be open after five minutes. Is everyone here already?

text.traditional: 中明說他快要到了。
text.simplified: 中明说他快要到了。
text.pinyin: Zhōngmíng shuō tā kuài yào dào le.
text.english: Zhongming said he’ll be here soon.

text.traditional: 老師，我們要不要先去排隊買票？
text.simplified: 老师，我们要不要先去排队买票？
text.pinyin: Lǎoshī, wǒmen yào bu yào xiān qù páiduì mǎi piào?
text.english: Teacher, should we get in line to buy tickets first?

text.traditional: 差不多需要排十分鐘的隊，那好吧，我們先去排隊。
text.simplified: 差不多需要排十分钟的队，那好吧，我们先去排队。
text.pinyin: Chàbuduō xūyào pái shí fēnzhōng de duì, nà hǎo ba, wǒmen xiān qù páiduì.
text.english: It takes about ten minutes to line up. Alright, let’s get in line to buy tickets first.

text.traditional: 今天我們打算參觀三個小時，會有人給我們介紹。進去以後，記得要安靜，不可以說話說得太大聲。
text.simplified: 今天我们打算参观三个小时，会有人给我们介绍。进去以后，记得要安静，不可以说话说得太大声。
text.pinyin: Jīntiān wǒmen dǎsuàn cānguān sān ge xiǎoshí, huì yǒu rén gěi wǒmen jièshào. Jìnqù yǐhòu, jìde yào ānjìng, bù kěyǐ shuōhuà shuō de tài dàshēng.
text.english: We plan to visit for three hours today. There will be someone introducing the museum for us. After you enter, remember to keep quiet. You can’t speak loudly.

text.traditional: 老師，我剛剛先用手機上網看了很多有趣的圖片，真想馬上就看到博物館裡的東西。
text.simplified: 老师，我刚刚先用手机上网看了很多有趣的图片，真想马上就看到博物馆里的东西。
text.pinyin: Lǎoshī, wǒ gānggāng xiān yòng shǒujī shàngwǎng kàn le hěn duō yǒuqù de túpiàn, zhēn xiǎng mǎshàng jiù kàndào bówùguǎn lǐ de dōngxi.
text.english: Teacher, I just used my cell phone to look for some information on the internet, and I saw many interesting pictures. I want to see what they have in the museum right away.

text.traditional: 我知道你非常喜歡歷史，我想你今天一定會很開心。
text.simplified: 我知道你非常喜欢历史，我想你今天一定会很开心。
text.pinyin: Wǒ zhīdào nǐ fēicháng xǐhuan lìshǐ, wǒ xiǎng nǐ jīntiān yídìng huì hěn kāixīn.
text.english: I know you like history very much. I think you’ll enjoy it a lot today.

text.traditional: 我也在網路上找了很多文章，那些介紹和故事都非常有趣。
text.simplified: 我也在网路上找了很多文章，那些介绍和故事都非常有趣。
text.pinyin: Wǒ yě zài wǎnglù shang zhǎo le hěn duō wénzhāng, nàxiē jièshào hé gùshi dōu fēicháng yǒuqù.
text.english: I also found many articles on the internet. Those introductions and stories are very fascinating.

text.traditional: 那如果大家有問題就可以問你了。
text.simplified: 那如果大家有问题就可以问你了。
text.pinyin: Nà rúguǒ dàjiā yǒu wèntí jiù kěyǐ wèn nǐ le.
text.english: If anyone has questions, they can ask you then.

text.traditional: 要是我知道，一定會告訴大家！
text.simplified: 要是我知道，一定会告诉大家！
text.pinyin: Yàoshi wǒ zhīdào, yídìng huì gàosu dàjiā!
text.english: If I know the answers, I’ll tell them for sure!

text.traditional: （往前看）中明來了！
text.simplified: （往前看）中明来了！
text.pinyin: (Wǎng qián kàn) Zhōngmíng lái le!
text.english: (Look forward) Here comes Zhongming!

text.traditional: 好，我們進去參觀吧。
text.simplified: 好，我们进去参观吧。
text.pinyin: Hǎo, wǒmen jìnqù cānguān ba.
text.english: Okay! Let’s get in to visit.

items.question: Where does 了 go when I say how long something lasted?
items.answer: Right after the action word. A 了 at the very end changes the meaning to 'still going on now'.

right.english: I rested for ten minutes.

words.meaning: ending word: something is done or has changed

items.question: My story is finished. Do I add a final 了 too?
items.answer: No. A finished time word like 去年 already closes the story. Use just one 了, right after the action.

right.english: Last year I lived for half a year.

items.question: Do I still need 了 if the time word already shows it is past?
items.answer: Yes. The time word shows WHEN; the 了 after the action shows the action is done.

right.pinyin: Zuótiān shuì le bā ge xiǎoshí.
right.english: He slept for eight hours yesterday.

timelineLab.title: Does the line end before NOW?
timelineLab.description: A finished story ends before now. The time word tells how long the action lasted.

choices.label: Last year
choices.traditional: 去年我在日本住了半年。
choices.simplified: 去年我在日本住了半年。
choices.pinyin: Qùnián wǒ zài Rìběn zhù le bànnián.
choices.english: Last year I lived in Japan for half a year.
choices.note: 去年 shows that the whole stay is inside a finished time.

choices.label: Yesterday
choices.traditional: 我昨天晚上看了兩個小時的書。
choices.simplified: 我昨天晚上看了两个小时的书。
choices.pinyin: Wǒ zuótiān wǎnshang kàn le liǎng ge xiǎoshí de shū.
choices.english: I studied for two hours last night.
choices.note: The study time is inside yesterday.

choices.label: Weekend
choices.traditional: 我們上週末打了兩個小時的籃球。
choices.simplified: 我们上周末打了两个小时的篮球。
choices.pinyin: Wǒmen shàng zhōumò dǎ le liǎng ge xiǎoshí de lánqiú.
choices.english: We played basketball for two hours last weekend.
choices.note: The finished weekend closes the story.

timelineLab.takeaway: This page says how long something lasted in a finished story. Context—not just the count of 了—closes the timeline.

examples.teachingNote: Duration expression with single 了 indicates a completed action in the past.

text.traditional: 去年我在日本住了半年。
text.simplified: 去年我在日本住了半年。
text.pinyin: Qùnián wǒ zài Rìběn zhù le bànnián.
text.english: Last year I lived in Japan for half a year.

examples.teachingNote: In dialogues, single 了 confirms the completed duration explaining current fatigue.

text.traditional: A: 你們為什麼都很累？ B: 因為我們昨天都工作了十個小時，所以今天都很累。
text.simplified: A: 你们为什么都很累？ B: 因为我们昨天都工作了十个小时，所以今天都很累。
text.pinyin: A: Nǐmen wèishénme dōu hěn lèi? B: Yīnwèi wǒmen zuótiān dōu gōngzuò le shí ge xiǎoshí, suǒyǐ jīntiān dōu hěn lèi.
text.english: A: Why are you all so tired? B: Because we all worked for ten hours yesterday, so today we are all very tired.

examples.teachingNote: 玩了十多天 indicates completed duration of vacation.

text.traditional: A: 我聽說上個月你去美國了。 B: 是啊，我在美國玩了十多天，上個週末回來的。
text.simplified: A: 我听说上个月你去美国了。 B: 是啊，我在美国玩了十多天，上个周末回来的。
text.pinyin: A: Wǒ tīngshuō shàng ge yuè nǐ qù Měiguó le. B: Shì a, wǒ zài Měiguó wán le shí duō tiān, shàng ge zhōumò huílái de.
text.english: A: I heard you went to the US last month. B: Yes, I had fun in the US for more than ten days, and came back last weekend.

grammarPages.titleTraditional: A 跟 B (不)一樣 (+ Vs)
grammarPages.titleEnglish: Compare Things with 跟…(不)一樣
grammarPages.learnerPromise: Say whether two things, customs, or ideas are the same or different.
grammarPages.explanation: Use 跟 between two things to compare them with 一樣 (the same) or 不一樣 (different). You can also add an adjective or descriptive verb at the end.

grammarPages.pattern: Thing A + 跟 + Thing B + (不)一樣 (+ Describing Word)

My thought is the same as his.
This book is just as interesting as that book.

items.question: Can I compare two things with 一樣 without 跟?
items.answer: No. When you mention the second item, use 跟 before it.
items.wrongTraditional: 越南的生肖中國的不一樣。
items.wrongSimplified: 越南的生肖中国的不一样。

right.traditional: 越南的生肖跟中國的不一樣。
right.simplified: 越南的生肖跟中国的不一样。
right.pinyin: Yuènán de shēngxiào gēn Zhōngguó de bù yíyàng.
right.english: Vietnam's zodiac is not the same as China's.

items.question: Does 不 go before 跟 or before 一樣?
items.answer: The negation 不 goes right in front of 一樣 (不一樣).
items.wrongTraditional: 越南的生肖不跟中國的一樣。
items.wrongSimplified: 越南的生肖不跟中国的一样。

right.traditional: 越南的生肖跟中國的不一樣。
right.simplified: 越南的生肖跟中国的不一样。
right.pinyin: Yuènán de shēngxiào gēn Zhōngguó de bù yíyàng.
right.english: Vietnam's zodiac is not the same as China's.

examples.teachingNote: 跟 links the two things being compared.

text.traditional: 越南的生肖跟中國的有點不一樣。
text.simplified: 越南的生肖跟中国的有点不一样。
text.pinyin: Yuènán de shēngxiào gēn Zhōngguó de yǒudiǎn bù yíyàng.
text.english: Vietnam's zodiac is a bit different from China's.

examples.teachingNote: Use 一樣 when two things share the exact same quality.

text.traditional: 他的想法跟我不一樣。
text.simplified: 他的想法跟我不一样。
text.pinyin: tā de xiǎngfǎ gēn wǒ bù yíyàng.
text.english: His idea is different from mine.

examples.teachingNote: Add a descriptive verb like 有意思 to say they are equally interesting.

text.traditional: 這本書跟那本書一樣有意思。
text.simplified: 这本书跟那本书一样有意思。
text.pinyin: zhè běn shū gēn nà běn shū yíyàng yǒuyìsi.
text.english: This book is just as interesting as that book.

examples.teachingNote: Ask if two things are the same using 嗎.

text.traditional: 日本的生肖跟台灣的一樣嗎？
text.simplified: 日本的生肖跟台湾的一样吗？
text.pinyin: Rìběn de shēngxiào gēn Táiwān de yíyàng ma?
text.english: Is Japan's zodiac the same as Taiwan's?

grammarPages.exercisePreview: State if things are the same or different
grammarPages.exerciseInstruction: Choose the correct word to compare the items.

segments.hint: Use 跟 to introduce the second item.

questions.correctFeedback: You compared the two zodiacs with 跟.
questions.repairFeedback: Use 跟 between the two items.

segments.hint: Say that they are not the same.

questions.correctFeedback: His idea is different from mine.
questions.repairFeedback: Choose 不一樣 for different ideas.

segments.hint: Say that both are equally interesting.

questions.correctFeedback: Both books are equally interesting.
questions.repairFeedback: Use 一樣 before the adjective.

dialogue.title: 十二生肖 · The Chinese Animal Zodiac
dialogue.setting: 對話一 · Dialogue 1

text.traditional: 我們下個星期要學第十五課，我剛才先看了一點，書上有很多種動物，我覺得很有意思。
text.simplified: 我们下个星期要学第十五课，我刚才先看了一点，书上有很多种动物，我觉得很有意思。
text.pinyin: Wǒmen xià ge xīngqí yào xué dì shíwǔ kè, wǒ gāngcái xiān kàn le yìdiǎn, shū shàng yǒu hěn duō zhǒng dòngwù, wǒ juéde hěn yǒuyìsi.
text.english: We are going to study Lesson 15 next week. I just glanced at it earlier. There are many kinds of animals in the book, which I think is very interesting.

text.traditional: 有哪些動物？
text.simplified: 有哪些动物？
text.pinyin: Yǒu nǎxiē dòngwù?
text.english: What animals are there?

text.traditional: 我記得有羊、馬、兔子，最特別的是龍。你看看！
text.simplified: 我记得有羊、马、兔子，最特别的是龙。你看看！
text.pinyin: Wǒ jìdé yǒu yáng, mǎ, tùzi, zuì tèbié de shì lóng. Nǐ kànkan!
text.english: I remember there are goats, horses, rabbits, and the most special one is the dragon. Take a look!

text.traditional: 原來是十二生肖，真的很有意思。
text.simplified: 原来是十二生肖，真的很有意思。
text.pinyin: Yuánlái shì shí'èr shēngxiào, zhēn de hěn yǒuyìsi.
text.english: Oh, so it’s the Chinese zodiac! That’s really fascinating.

text.traditional: 什麼是十二生肖？
text.simplified: 什么是十二生肖？
text.pinyin: Shénme shì shí'èr shēngxiào?
text.english: What is the Chinese zodiac?

text.traditional: 華人用不一樣的動物代表每一年，一共有十二種動物。
text.simplified: 华人用不一样的动物代表每一年，一共有十二种动物。
text.pinyin: Huárén yòng bù yíyàng de dòngwù dàibiǎo měi yì nián, yígòng yǒu shí'èr zhǒng dòngwù.
text.english: Chinese people use different animals to represent each year. There are twelve animals in total.

text.traditional: 越南也有十二生肖，可是我們沒有兔年，有貓年。我是貓年出生的，屬貓。
text.simplified: 越南也有十二生肖，可是我们没有兔年，有猫年。我是猫年出生的，属猫。
text.pinyin: Yuènán yě yǒu shí'èr shēngxiào, kěshì wǒmen méiyǒu tùnián, yǒu māonián. Wǒ shì māonián chūshēng de, shǔ māo.
text.english: Vietnam also has the twelve zodiac animals, but we don't have the Year of the Rabbit; we have the Year of the Cat. I was born in the Year of the Cat, so my zodiac sign is the cat.

text.traditional: 真的？好有趣！原來越南的生肖跟中國的有點不一樣。我好想知道我屬什麼。
text.simplified: 真的？好有趣！原来越南的生肖跟中国的有点不一样。我好想知道我属什么。
text.pinyin: Zhēn de? Hǎo yǒuqù! Yuánlái Yuènán de shēngxiào gēn Zhōngguó de yǒudiǎn bù yíyàng. Wǒ hǎo xiǎng zhīdào wǒ shǔ shénme.
text.english: Really? How interesting! It turns out Vietnam's zodiac is a bit different from China's. I really want to know what sign I am.

text.traditional: 很簡單，上網一查就知道了。
text.simplified: 很简单，上网一查就知道了。
text.pinyin: Hěn jiǎndān, shàngwǎng yì chá jiù zhīdào le.
text.english: It's very simple. Just look it up online and you'll know immediately.

text.traditional: 好，我上網查查看。
text.simplified: 好，我上网查查看。
text.pinyin: Hǎo, wǒ shàngwǎng cháchá kàn.
text.english: Okay, I'll search for it online.

comprehension.prompt: 越南的生肖有什麼特別的地方？
comprehension.hint: Listen to Yuanzhen talk about Vietnam's zodiac.

items.title: Grammar 2 · Describe Ongoing States with 著

grammarPages.titleTraditional: S + V1 + 著 + (O1) + V2 + O2 (狀態持續)
grammarPages.titleEnglish: Describe an Ongoing State with 著
grammarPages.learnerPromise: Describe an ongoing posture, holding state, or background action.
grammarPages.explanation: The particle 著 attaches to a verb (like 拿著, 放著, 坐著) to show that the physical position or state continues, often as the background while another action happens.

teachingGlossary.meaning: ending word: something is done or has changed
link word that connects a describing word to a thing
to have a holiday or vacation

grammarPages.pattern: Subject / Place + Verb + 著 + Object (+ Next Action)

patternRows.english: What are you holding in your hand?
A few animal figures are placed on the table.
Many adults brought children to see the lantern show.

items.question: What is the difference between 正在 and 著?
items.answer: 正在 describes an ongoing dynamic action (e.g. 正在吃). 著 describes a static continuous state or posture (e.g. 拿著, 放著, 坐著).

right.english: He is holding a lantern in his hand.

items.question: Where does 著 attach in the sentence?
items.answer: 著 attaches directly right after the verb that describes the posture or state (拿著, 放著).

right.english: He is holding a lantern in his hand.

examples.teachingNote: 拿著 describes holding something continuously.

text.traditional: 中明，你手裡拿著什麼？
text.simplified: 中明，你手里拿着什么？
text.pinyin: Zhōngmíng, nǐ shǒu lǐ názhe shénme?
text.english: Zhongming, what are you holding in your hand?

examples.teachingNote: 放著 describes an object resting in a position.

text.traditional: 桌上放著幾隻用紙做的動物。
text.simplified: 桌上放着几只用纸做的动物。
text.pinyin: zhuō shàng fàngzhe jǐ zhī yòng zhǐ zuò de dòngwù.
text.english: Several animals made of paper were sitting on the table.

examples.teachingNote: 帶著 describes bringing or accompanying someone.

text.traditional: 很多大人帶著小孩去看燈會。
text.simplified: 很多大人带着小孩去看灯会。
text.pinyin: hěn duō dàrén dàizhe xiǎohái qù kàn dēnghuì.
text.english: Many adults brought children along to see the lantern festival.

examples.teachingNote: 門上開著 / 牆上貼著 shows an ongoing display on a surface.

text.traditional: 黑板上貼著很多張動物的圖片。
text.simplified: 黑板上贴着很多张动物的图片。
text.pinyin: hēibǎn shàng tiēzhe hěn duō zhāng dòngwù de túpiàn.
text.english: Many pictures of animals were posted on the blackboard.

grammarPages.exercisePreview: Show what continues in a position
grammarPages.exerciseInstruction: Pick the verb form with 著 to describe the state.

segments.hint: Describe what is held in the hand.

questions.correctFeedback: Holding something in the hand.
questions.repairFeedback: Use 拿著 for holding.

segments.hint: Describe items placed on the desk.

questions.correctFeedback: The items are resting on the desk.
questions.repairFeedback: Use 放著 for placed items.

segments.hint: Describe bringing children along.

questions.correctFeedback: Adults bringing children along.
questions.repairFeedback: Use 帶著 for bringing someone.

dialogue.title: 十二生肖 · The Chinese Animal Zodiac
dialogue.setting: 對話二 · Dialogue 2

text.traditional: 中明，你手裡拿著什麼？
text.simplified: 中明，你手里拿着什么？
text.pinyin: Zhōngmíng, nǐ shǒulǐ názhe shénme?
text.english: Zhongming, what are you holding in your hand?

text.traditional: 這是燈籠。
text.simplified: 这是灯笼。
text.pinyin: Zhè shì dēnglóng.
text.english: This is a lantern.

text.traditional: 燈籠上的小老虎好可愛。
text.simplified: 灯笼上的小老虎好可爱。
text.pinyin: Dēnglóng shàng de xiǎo lǎohǔ hǎo kě'ài.
text.english: The little tiger on the lantern is so cute.

text.traditional: 這是我朋友做的，因為他屬虎。你知道十二生肖嗎？
text.simplified: 这是我朋友做的，因为他属虎。你知道十二生肖吗？
text.pinyin: Zhè shì wǒ péngyǒu zuò de, yīnwèi tā shǔ hǔ. Nǐ zhīdào shí'èr shēngxiào ma?
text.english: A friend of mine made it because he was born in the year of the tiger. Do you know about the twelve zodiac animals?

text.traditional: 知道，友美跟我講過。
text.simplified: 知道，友美跟我讲过。
text.pinyin: Zhīdào, Yǒuměi gēn wǒ jiǎng guò.
text.english: Yes, Youmei mentioned it to me.

text.traditional: 這個星期六是元宵節，你跟友美會去看燈會嗎？
text.simplified: 这个星期六是元宵节，你跟友美会去看灯会吗？
text.pinyin: Zhège xīngqíliù shì Yuánxiāojié, nǐ gēn Yǒuměi huì qù kàn dēnghuì ma?
text.english: This Saturday is the Lantern Festival. Are you and Youmei going to see the lantern show?

text.traditional: 友美說她想去，我還沒決定去不去。燈會好玩嗎？
text.simplified: 友美说她想去，我还没决定去不去。灯会好玩吗？
text.pinyin: Yǒuměi shuō tā xiǎng qù, wǒ hái méi juédìng qù bú qù. Dēnghuì hǎowán ma?
text.english: Youmei said she wants to go, but I haven't decided yet. Is the lantern festival fun?

text.traditional: 我去年去看了，很多大人帶著小孩去看燈會，非常熱鬧。我照了很多相片。
text.simplified: 我去年去看了，很多大人带着小孩去看灯会，非常热闹。我照了很多相片。
text.pinyin: Wǒ qùnián qù kàn le, hěn duō dàrén dàizhe xiǎohái qù kàn dēnghuì, fēicháng rènào. Wǒ zhào le hěn duō xiàngpiàn.
text.english: I went last year. Many adults brought their kids to see the lantern show; it was very lively. I took a lot of pictures.

text.traditional: 那我這個週末一定要去看看。
text.simplified: 那我这个周末一定要去看看。
text.pinyin: Nà wǒ zhège zhōumò yídìng yào qù kànkan.
text.english: Then I must definitely go see it this weekend.

text.traditional: 我週末還要工作，打算一下班就去看燈會。我們可以約友美一起去。
text.simplified: 我周末还要工作，打算一下班就去看灯会。我们可以约友美一起去。
text.pinyin: Wǒ zhōumò hái yào gōngzuò, dǎsuàn yí xiàbān jiù qù kàn dēnghuì. Wǒmen kěyǐ yuē Yǒuměi yìqǐ qù.
text.english: I have to work this weekend, but I plan to go see the lantern show right after getting off work. We can invite Youmei to join us.

items.title: Grammar 3 · Immediate Sequence with 一……就……

grammarPages.titleEnglish: Express Immediate Sequence with 一……就……
grammarPages.learnerPromise: Say that as soon as one action happened, another followed immediately.
grammarPages.explanation: Put 一 before the first action and 就 before the second action to express 'as soon as... then...'. It emphasizes how quickly and immediately the second event occurs.

teachingGlossary.meaning: ending word: something is done or has changed
link word that connects a describing word to a thing
to have a holiday or vacation

grammarPages.pattern: Subject + 一 + Verb 1 + 就 + Verb 2

patternRows.english: As soon as you search online, you will know.

grammar.meaning: as soon as get off work

patternRows.english: As soon as I get off work, I will go see the lantern show.
As soon as I entered the classroom today, I saw the animals.

items.question: Can I omit 一 or 就?
items.answer: No. The two markers work as a pair: 一 marks the trigger, and 就 marks the immediate action that follows.

right.pinyin: shàngwǎng yì chá jiù zhīdào le.
right.english: As soon as you look it up online, you will know.

items.question: Which action does 一 go with?
items.answer: 一 always attaches before the first action, and 就 goes before the second action.

right.pinyin: shàngwǎng yì chá jiù zhīdào le.
right.english: As soon as you look it up online, you will know.

examples.teachingNote: 一查就知道了 shows how effortless and immediate the answer is.

text.traditional: 很簡單，上網一查就知道了。
text.simplified: 很简单，上网一查就知道了。
text.pinyin: hěn jiǎndān, shàngwǎng yì chá jiù zhīdào le.
text.english: It's very simple: as soon as you search online, you will know.

examples.teachingNote: 一下班就去看 shows immediate intention right after finishing work.

text.traditional: 我打算一下班就去看燈會。
text.simplified: 我打算一下班就去看灯会。
text.pinyin: wǒ dǎsuàn yí xiàbān jiù qù kàn dēnghuì.
text.english: I plan to go see the lantern show right after getting off work.

words.meaning: as soon as get off work

examples.teachingNote: 一進教室就看到 tells the narrative of an immediate discovery upon entering.

text.traditional: 今天一進教室，就看到桌上放著幾隻動物。
text.simplified: 今天一进教室，就看到桌上放着几只动物。
text.pinyin: jīntiān yí jìn jiàoshì, jiù kàndào zhuō shàng fàngzhe jǐ zhī dòngwù.
text.english: As soon as I entered the classroom today, I saw several animals placed on the table.

examples.teachingNote: 一到就打電話 shows sequence of arrival and contacting someone.

text.traditional: 他一到家，就給我打電話了。
text.simplified: 他一到家，就给我打电话了。
text.pinyin: tā yí dào jiā, jiù gěi wǒ dǎ diànhuà le.
text.english: As soon as he arrived home, he called me.

grammarPages.exercisePreview: Express immediate successive actions
grammarPages.exerciseInstruction: Choose 一 or 就 to link the two actions.

segments.hint: Use 一 before the first quick action.

questions.correctFeedback: As soon as you search, you know.
questions.repairFeedback: Use 一 before the action.

segments.hint: Use 就 before the immediate next action.

questions.correctFeedback: Going right after work.
questions.repairFeedback: Use 就 before the next action.

segments.hint: As soon as entering the classroom.

segments.traditional: 教室，就看到桌上放著動物。

questions.correctFeedback: Immediately upon entering.
questions.repairFeedback: Pair 一 with the entering verb.

dialogue.title: 有趣的十二生肖 · The Interesting Zodiac
dialogue.setting: 短文 · Reading

text.traditional: 今天一進教室，就看到桌上放著幾隻用紙做的動物，黑板上也有很多張動物的圖片，我覺得很有趣。
text.simplified: 今天一进教室，就看到桌上放着几只用纸做的动物，黑板上也有很多张动物的图片，我觉得很有趣。
text.pinyin: Jīntiān yí jìn jiàoshì, jiù kàndào zhuō shàng fàngzhe jǐ zhī yòng zhǐ zuò de dòngwù, hēibǎn shàng yě yǒu hěn duō zhāng dòngwù de túpiàn, wǒ juéde hěn yǒuqù.
text.english: As soon as I walked into the classroom today, I saw several paper animals placed on the table, and there were also many pictures of animals on the blackboard. I found it very interesting.

text.traditional: 老師告訴我們，很久以前，有十二種動物一起參加了一個過河比賽，看誰游得最快。
text.simplified: 老师告诉我们，很久以前，有十二种动物一起参加了一个过河比赛，看谁游得最快。
text.pinyin: Lǎoshī gàosu wǒmen, hěn jiǔ yǐqián, yǒu shí'èr zhǒng dòngwù yìqǐ cānjiā le yí ge guòhé bǐsài, kàn shéi yóu de zuì kuài.
text.english: The teacher told us that a long time ago, twelve animals entered a river-crossing race together to see who could swim the fastest.

text.traditional: 開始比賽以後，每隻動物都游得很快很辛苦。老鼠先過了河，第二個到的是牛，最後到的是豬。老鼠贏了，排第一，其他動物排後面。
text.simplified: 开始比赛以后，每只动物都游得很快很辛苦。老鼠先过了河，第二个到的是牛，最后到的是猪。老鼠赢了，排第一，其他动物排后面。
text.pinyin: Kāishǐ bǐsài yǐhòu, měi zhī dòngwù dōu yóu de hěn kuài hěn xīnkǔ. Lǎoshǔ xiān guò le hé, dì èr ge dào de shì niú, zuìhòu dào de shì zhū. Lǎoshǔ yíng le, pái dì yī, qítā dòngwù pái hòumiàn.
text.english: After the race began, each animal swam hard and fast. The rat crossed the river first, the ox arrived second, and the pig arrived last. The rat won, ranking first, and the other animals lined up behind.

text.traditional: 這次比賽以後，華人就用鼠、牛、虎、兔、龍、蛇、馬、羊、猴、雞、狗和豬代表每一年，而且叫這十二種動物「十二生肖」。
text.simplified: 这次比赛以后，华人就用鼠、牛、虎、兔、龙、蛇、马、羊、猴、鸡、狗和猪代表每一年，而且叫这十二种动物「十二生肖」。
text.pinyin: Zhè cì bǐsài yǐhòu, Huárén jiù yòng shǔ, niú, hǔ, tù, lóng, shé, mǎ, yáng, hóu, jī, gǒu hé zhū dàibiǎo měi yì nián, érqiě jiào zhè shí'èr zhǒng dòngwù "shí'èr shēngxiào".
text.english: After this race, Chinese people used the rat, ox, tiger, rabbit, dragon, snake, horse, goat, monkey, rooster, dog, and pig to represent each year, calling these twelve animals the "Twelve Zodiac Animals".

text.traditional: 華人聊天的時候，會問別人「你屬什麼？」。每年到了元宵節，代表那年的動物燈籠，也會最受歡迎。
text.simplified: 华人聊天的时候，会问别人「你属什么？」。每年到了元宵节，代表那年的动物灯笼，也会最受欢迎。
text.pinyin: Huárén liáotiān de shíhou, huì wèn biérén "nǐ shǔ shénme?". Měi nián dào le Yuánxiāojié, dàibiǎo nà nián de dòngwù dēnglóng, yě huì zuì shòu huānyíng.
text.english: When chatting, Chinese people often ask others, "What is your zodiac sign?". Every year during the Lantern Festival, the lantern representing the animal of that year is also the most popular.

comprehension.hint: The reading states which animal crossed first.

items.title: Grammar 1 · Distances with 離

grammarPages.titleEnglish: Say How Close or Far Two Places Are with 離
grammarPages.learnerPromise: Say how close or far one place is from another.
grammarPages.explanation: 離 says the distance from one place to another. Put 很近 (very close) or 很遠 (very far) after the second place.

teachingGlossary.meaning: ending word: something is done or has changed
link word that connects a describing word to a thing
to have a holiday or vacation

grammarPages.pattern: Place A + 離 + Place B + 很 (近／遠)

patternRows.english: The train station is very close to the department store.
The school is far from the hospital.
My home is very close to the park.

items.question: Can I say how far two places are without 離?
items.answer: No. 離 is the word that names the distance. Without it, the sentence does not compare two places.

right.traditional: 火車站離百貨公司很近。
right.simplified: 火车站离百货公司很近。
right.pinyin: huǒchē zhàn lí bǎihuò gōngsī hěn jìn。
right.english: The train station is very close to the department store.

items.question: What is the difference between 離 and 從?
items.answer: 離 tells a distance between two places. 從 tells where a trip starts. Use 離 for distance.

right.english: The school is far from the hospital.

items.question: Where does 很近 go in the sentence?
items.answer: Right after the second place. The pattern is Place A 離 Place B 很近.
items.wrongTraditional: 離火車站百貨公司很近。
items.wrongSimplified: 离火车站百货公司很近。

right.traditional: 火車站離百貨公司很近。
right.simplified: 火车站离百货公司很近。
right.pinyin: huǒchē zhàn lí bǎihuò gōngsī hěn jìn。
right.english: The train station is very close to the department store.

examples.teachingNote: 離 names the distance from place A to place B.

text.traditional: 火車站離百貨公司很近。
text.simplified: 火车站离百货公司很近。
text.pinyin: huǒchē zhàn lí bǎihuò gōngsī hěn jìn。
text.english: The train station is very close to the department store.

examples.teachingNote: 很遠 goes at the end of the pattern.

text.traditional: 學校離醫院很遠。
text.simplified: 学校离医院很远。
text.pinyin: xuéxiào lí yīyuàn hěn yuǎn。
text.english: The school is far from the hospital.

examples.teachingNote: The places can be anything: buildings, parks, or home.

text.traditional: 我家離公園很近。
text.simplified: 我家离公园很近。
text.pinyin: wǒ jiā lí gōngyuán hěn jìn。
text.english: My home is very close to the park.

grammarPages.exercisePreview: Put 離 and 很近 or 很遠 into the sentence.
grammarPages.exerciseInstruction: Finish each sentence about distance.

segments.hint: Use 離 between the two places.

dialogue.title: 在台灣旅行 · Traveling in Taiwan
dialogue.setting: 對話一 · Dialogue 1

text.traditional: 國安，這次學校放假，你有什麼計畫？
text.simplified: 国安，这次学校放假，你有什么计划？
text.pinyin: Guó'ān, zhè cì xuéxiào fàngjià, nǐ yǒu shénme jìhuà?
text.english: Guo'an, school is going on vacation this time. Do you have any plans?

text.traditional: 我還沒打算要做什麼。這次放假，沒有上次放得那麼久，只放三天假，我不知道去哪裡比較好。
text.simplified: 我还没打算要做什么。这次放假，没有上次放得那么久，只放三天假，我不知道去哪里比较好。
text.pinyin: Wǒ hái méi dǎsuàn yào zuò shénme. Zhè cì fàngjià, méiyǒu shàng cì fàng de nàme jiǔ, zhǐ fàng sān tiān jià, wǒ bù zhīdào qù nǎlǐ bǐjiào hǎo.
text.english: I haven't decided what to do yet. This break is not as long as the last one—only three days—so I don't know where it's best to go.

text.traditional: 我覺得太魯閣不錯，有山又有河。
text.simplified: 我觉得太鲁阁不错，有山又有河。
text.pinyin: Wǒ juéde Tàilǔgé búcuò, yǒu shān yòu yǒu hé.
text.english: I think Taroko Gorge is great; it has both mountains and rivers.

text.traditional: 在哪裡？離台北遠不遠？
text.simplified: 在哪里？离台北远不远？
text.pinyin: Zài nǎlǐ? Lí Táiběi yuǎn bù yuǎn?
text.english: Where is it? Is it far from Taipei?

text.traditional: 在花蓮。花蓮在台灣東部，離台北有點遠，你可以坐火車去，也可以開車去，差不多四個小時。
text.simplified: 在花莲。花莲在台湾东部，离台北有点远，你可以坐火车去，也可以开车去，差不多四个小时。
text.pinyin: Zài Huālián. Huālián zài Táiwān dōngbù, lí Táiběi yǒudiǎn yuǎn, nǐ kěyǐ zuò huǒchē qù, yě kěyǐ kāichē qù, chàbùduō sì ge xiǎoshí.
text.english: It's in Hualien. Hualien is in eastern Taiwan, somewhat far from Taipei. You can take a train or drive there; it takes about four hours.

text.traditional: 你去過嗎？
text.simplified: 你去过吗？
text.pinyin: Nǐ qù guò ma?
text.english: Have you been there?

text.traditional: 我小學六年級的時候去過，我很喜歡那裡。
text.simplified: 我小学六年级的时候去过，我很喜欢那里。
text.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎoxué liù niánjí de shíhou qù guò, wǒ hěn xǐhuān nàlǐ.
text.english: I went when I was in sixth grade of elementary school. I liked it very much.

text.traditional: 那你打算去哪裡玩？
text.simplified: 那你打算去哪里玩？
text.pinyin: Nà nǐ dǎsuàn qù nǎlǐ wán?
text.english: Where do you plan to go for fun?

text.traditional: 我想去合歡山。報紙上寫，這幾天可能會下雪。
text.simplified: 我想去合欢山。报纸上写，这几天可能会下雪。
text.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng qù Héhuān Shān. Bàozhǐ shàng xiě, zhè jǐ tiān kěnéng huì xiàxuě.
text.english: I want to go to Hehuanshan. The newspaper says it might snow these few days.

text.traditional: 下雪？我還沒看過雪，合歡山在哪裡？
text.simplified: 下雪？我还没看过雪，合欢山在哪里？
text.pinyin: Xiàxuě? Wǒ hái méi kàn guò xuě, Héhuān Shān zài nǎlǐ?
text.english: Snow? I haven't seen snow before. Where is Hehuanshan?

text.traditional: 在台灣的中部，日月潭也在附近。
text.simplified: 在台湾的中部，日月潭也在附近。
text.pinyin: Zài Táiwān de zhōngbù, Rìyuè Tán yě zài fùjìn.
text.english: In central Taiwan. Sun Moon Lake is also nearby.

text.traditional: 日月潭很有名，我在書上看過，離合歡山近嗎？
text.simplified: 日月潭很有名，我在书上看过，离合欢山近吗？
text.pinyin: Rìyuè Tán hěn yǒumíng, wǒ zài shū shàng kàn guò, lí Héhuān Shān jìn ma?
text.english: Sun Moon Lake is very famous. I read about it in a book. Is it close to Hehuanshan?

text.traditional: 不遠，我想去玩三天兩夜，先去日月潭，再去合歡山。
text.simplified: 不远，我想去玩三天两夜，先去日月潭，再去合欢山。
text.pinyin: Bù yuǎn, wǒ xiǎng qù wán sān tiān liǎng yè, xiān qù Rìyuè Tán, zài qù Héhuān Shān.
text.english: Not far. I want to go for three days and two nights: go to Sun Moon Lake first, and then to Hehuanshan.

text.traditional: 你記得多照一些相片給我看！
text.simplified: 你记得多照一些相片给我看！
text.pinyin: Nǐ jìdé duō zhào yìxiē xiàngpiàn gěi wǒ kàn!
text.english: Remember to take more pictures for me to see!

items.title: Grammar 2–5 · Changes, Comparatives, Sequences, and Complements

grammarPages.titleEnglish: Say What Changed from Before with 本來 (原來) … 後來 …
grammarPages.learnerPromise: Say how things were before and what changed.
grammarPages.explanation: 本來 (or 原來) tells how things were at first. 後來 tells what changed after. The two parts work together to show a change.

teachingGlossary.meaning: ending word: something is done or has changed
link word that connects a describing word to a thing
to have a holiday or vacation

grammarPages.pattern: S + 本來 + first part，後來 + changed part

complement.meaning: ending word: something is done or has changed

patternRows.english: At first he had no car. Later he bought one.

complement.meaning: ending word: something is done or has changed

patternRows.english: At first I wanted to see a movie. Later it rained.

complement.meaning: ending word: something is done or has changed

patternRows.english: We first had three dogs. Later we gave one to a friend.

items.question: Do 本來 and 原來 mean the same thing?
items.answer: Yes, for showing how things were at first. Use either one at the start of the changed story.

right.traditional: 他本來沒有車，後來買車了。
right.simplified: 他本来没有车，后来买车了。
right.pinyin: tā běnlái méiyǒu chē， hòulái mǎi chē le。
right.english: At first he had no car. Later he bought one.

words.meaning: ending word: something is done or has changed

items.question: Do I keep 來 or 了 at the very end?
items.answer: The changed part ends with 了. 後來 sits before the changed part, not at the end.
items.wrongTraditional: 他本來沒有車，後來買車來。
items.wrongSimplified: 他本来没有车，后来买车来。

right.traditional: 他本來沒有車，後來買車了。
right.simplified: 他本来没有车，后来买车了。
right.pinyin: tā běnlái méiyǒu chē， hòulái mǎi chē le。
right.english: At first he had no car. Later he bought one.

words.meaning: ending word: something is done or has changed

items.question: Can I use only 後來 to show a change?
items.answer: A change story reads better with both parts. 本來 (or 原來) starts it, and 後來 gives the change.

right.traditional: 他本來沒有車，後來買車了。
right.simplified: 他本来没有车，后来买车了。
right.pinyin: tā běnlái méiyǒu chē， hòulái mǎi chē le。
right.english: At first he had no car. Later he bought one.

words.meaning: ending word: something is done or has changed

examples.teachingNote: 本來 starts the first plan; 後來 gives what changed.

text.traditional: 我今天本來想去看電影，後來下雨就沒去了。
text.simplified: 我今天本来想去看电影，后来下雨就没去了。
text.pinyin: wǒ jīntiān běnlái xiǎng qù kàn diànyǐng， hòulái xià yǔ jiù méi qù le。
text.english: I first wanted to see a movie today, but then it rained so I did not go.

text.traditional: 我家原來有三隻狗，後來一隻送朋友了。
text.simplified: 我家原来有三只狗，后来一只送朋友了。
text.pinyin: wǒ jiā yuánlái yǒu sān zhī gǒu， hòulái yì zhī sòng péngyǒu le。
text.english: We first had three dogs; later we gave one to a friend.

grammarPages.titleEnglish: Compare Two Things as Even More with 更
grammarPages.learnerPromise: Say that one thing is even more so than another.
grammarPages.explanation: 比 compares two things. 更 makes the second thing stronger. The shape is: thing one + 比 + thing two + 更 + a describing word.

teachingGlossary.meaning: ending word: something is done or has changed
link word that connects a describing word to a thing
to have a holiday or vacation

grammarPages.pattern: Thing one + 比 + thing two + 更 + describing word

patternRows.english: Today is even colder than yesterday.
Family is even more important than friends.
He is even smarter than I am.

items.question: Can I compare with only 更?
items.answer: For a two-thing comparison you also need 比. The shape is thing 比 thing 更 + describing word.

right.english: Today is even colder than yesterday.

items.question: Where does 更 go?
items.answer: Right before the describing word. It is not after the second thing.

right.english: Today is even colder than yesterday.

items.question: Does 更 mean the most?
items.answer: No. 更 means even more between two things. Say 最 for the most among a group.

right.english: Today is even colder than yesterday.

examples.teachingNote: 比 shows the two things; 更 makes the second stronger.

text.traditional: 今天比昨天更冷。
text.simplified: 今天比昨天更冷。
text.pinyin: jīntiān bǐ zuótiān gèng lěng。
text.english: Today is even colder than yesterday.

examples.teachingNote: The comparing word is 更, not 很.

text.traditional: 我覺得家人比朋友更重要。
text.simplified: 我觉得家人比朋友更重要。
text.pinyin: wǒ juéde jiārén bǐ péngyǒu gèng zhòngyào。
text.english: I feel that family is even more important than friends.

examples.teachingNote: Any two people or things can be compared with 比 and 更.

text.traditional: 他比我更聰明。
text.simplified: 他比我更聪明。
text.pinyin: tā bǐ wǒ gèng cōngming。
text.english: He is even smarter than me.

grammarPages.titleEnglish: Link Two Finished Actions with 就
grammarPages.learnerPromise: Say what happened right after an action was finished.
grammarPages.explanation: Finish one action (verb + 了) and add 就 before the next action. The next thing happens right away.

teachingGlossary.meaning: ending word: something is done or has changed
link word that connects a describing word to a thing
to have a holiday or vacation

grammarPages.pattern: First action (verb + 了) + just now + next action

ending word: something is done or has changed

items.question: Where does the first 了 go?
items.answer: Right after the first action. 就 comes before the next action.

words.meaning: ending word: something is done or has changed
ending word: something is done or has changed

items.question: Do I need 就 between the two actions?
items.answer: Yes. 就 is the word that links the finished action to what happened right after.

right.pinyin: tā fàng le jià， jiù qù lǚxíng le。
right.english: As soon as his holiday began, he went traveling.

words.meaning: ending word: something is done or has changed
ending word: something is done or has changed

items.question: Do both actions need 了?
items.answer: The first action takes 了 to show it is finished. The next action may also end with 了.

right.pinyin: tā fàng le jià， jiù qù lǚxíng le。
right.english: As soon as his holiday began, he went traveling.

words.meaning: ending word: something is done or has changed
ending word: something is done or has changed
